5.24.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tatra viṣṇupadaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ tīrthe śubhe sthitam ..
aparaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvapātakanāśanam .. 1 ..
5.24.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तत्र विष्णुपदं नाम तीर्थं तीर्थे शुभे स्थितम् ..
अपरं ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठाः सर्वपातकनाशनम् .. 1 ..
5.24.m: Sūta said: / There, situated in that auspicious sacred ford, is another sacred ford named Viṣṇupada, / O best of brahmins, destroying all serious sins.

5.24.s:
ayane dakṣiṇe prāpte yastatpūjya samāhitaḥ ..
nivedayettathātmānaṃ samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ .. 2 ..
5.24.d:
अयने दक्षिणे प्राप्ते यस्तत्पूज्य समाहितः ..
निवेदयेत्तथात्मानं सम्यक्छ्रद्धासमन्वितः .. 2 ..
5.24.m: When the southern solstice has arrived, he who, with concentrated mind, / worships it and surrenders himself with full faith,

5.24.s:
sa mṛto'pyayane yāmye tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ..
prāpnoti nātra saṃdehastatprabhāvāddvijottamāḥ .. 3 ..
5.24.d:
स मृतोऽप्ययने याम्ये तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ..
प्राप्नोति नात्र संदेहस्तत्प्रभावाद्द्विजोत्तमाः .. 3 ..
5.24.m: even if he dies during the southern solstice, / reaches that supreme abode of Viṣṇu; there is no doubt of this, O best of brahmins, through its power.

5.24.s:
tathā caivottare prāpte pūjayitvā yathāvidhi ..
samyaṅnivedayedbhaktyā ātmānaṃ yaḥ samāhitaḥ ..
so'pi viṣṇoḥ padaṃ puṇyaṃ prāpya saṃjāyate sukhī .. 4 ..
5.24.d:
तथा चैवोत्तरे प्राप्ते पूजयित्वा यथाविधि ..
सम्यङ्निवेदयेद्भक्त्या आत्मानं यः समाहितः ..
सोऽपि विष्णोः पदं पुण्यं प्राप्य संजायते सुखी .. 4 ..
5.24.m: And likewise, when the northern [solstice] has arrived, having worshipped according to rule, / he who, concentrated, properly surrenders himself with devotion, / he too, reaching the holy abode of Viṣṇu, becomes happy.

5.24.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
kathaṃ tatra padaṃ jātaṃ viṣṇoravyaktajanmanaḥ ..
kathaṃ nivedyate tatra samyagātmā' yanadvaye .. 5 ..
5.24.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
कथं तत्र पदं जातं विष्णोरव्यक्तजन्मनः ..
कथं निवेद्यते तत्र सम्यगात्मा' यनद्वये .. 5 ..
5.24.m: The seers said: / How did the footprint of Viṣṇu, whose birth is unmanifest, arise there? / How is oneself properly surrendered there at the two solstices?

5.24.s:
tasmindṛṣṭe'thavā spṛṣṭe yatphalaṃ labhyate naraiḥ ..
tatsarvaṃ sūtaja brūhi paraṃ kautṛhalaṃ hi naḥ .. 6 ..
5.24.d:
तस्मिन्दृष्टेऽथवा स्पृष्टे यत्फलं लभ्यते नरैः ..
तत्सर्वं सूतज ब्रूहि परं कौतृहलं हि नः .. 6 ..
5.24.m: Tell all that, O son of Sūta, which fruit is obtained by men / when it is seen or touched, for our curiosity is indeed great.

5.24.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
balirbaddho yadā tena viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā ..
tadā kramaistribhirvyāptaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram .. 7 ..
5.24.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
बलिर्बद्धो यदा तेन विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ..
तदा क्रमैस्त्रिभिर्व्याप्तं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् .. 7 ..
5.24.m: Sūta said: / When Bali was bound by that mighty Viṣṇu, / then the three worlds, with moving and unmoving beings, were pervaded by [his] three strides.

5.24.s:
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre saṃnyastaḥ prathamaḥ kramaḥ ..
maharloke dvitī yastu tadā tena mahātmanā .. 8 ..
5.24.d:
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे संन्यस्तः प्रथमः क्रमः ..
महर्लोके द्विती यस्तु तदा तेन महात्मना .. 8 ..
5.24.m: The first stride was placed in the sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara, / and the second in Maharloka by that great-souled one at that time.

5.24.s:
tṛtīyasya samudyogaṃ yadā cakre sa cakradhṛk ..
tadā bhinnaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhā brahmāṃḍaṃ laghutāṃ gatam .. 9 ..
5.24.d:
तृतीयस्य समुद्योगं यदा चक्रे स चक्रधृक् ..
तदा भिन्नं द्विजश्रेष्ठा ब्रह्मांडं लघुतां गतम् .. 9 ..
5.24.m: When the discus-bearer made the effort for the third [stride], / then the cosmic egg was pierced, O best of twice-born, and attained lightness.

5.24.s:
pādāgreṇātha saṃbhinne brahmāṃḍe nirmalaṃ jalam ..
aṃguṣṭhāgreṇa saṃprāptaṃ krameṇa dharaṇītale .. 6.24.10 ..
5.24.d:
पादाग्रेणाथ संभिन्ने ब्रह्मांडे निर्मलं जलम् ..
अंगुष्ठाग्रेण संप्राप्तं क्रमेण धरणीतले .. 6.24.10 ..
5.24.m: Then, when the cosmic egg was pierced by the tip of his foot, the clear water / reached the surface of the earth in due order by the tip of his big toe.

5.24.s:
brahmalokaṃ tadā kṛtsnaṃ plāvayitvā jalaṃ hi tat ..
śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ kundendusadṛśadyuti ..
matsyakacchapasaṃkīrṇaṃ grāhayūthaiḥ samākulam .. 11 ..
5.24.d:
ब्रह्मलोकं तदा कृत्स्नं प्लावयित्वा जलं हि तत् ..
शुद्धस्फटिकसंकाशं कुन्देन्दुसदृशद्युति ..
मत्स्यकच्छपसंकीर्णं ग्राहयूथैः समाकुलम् .. 11 ..
5.24.m: Indeed, that water, having then flooded the entire world of Brahmā, / resembling pure crystal, with a luster like jasmine and the moon, / filled with fish and turtles, crowded with hosts of crocodiles,

5.24.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti sā loke gaṃgā viṣṇupadī smṛtā ..
pavitramapi tatkṣetraṃ nayantī sā pavitratām .. 12 ..
5.24.d:
ततः प्रभृति सा लोके गंगा विष्णुपदी स्मृता ..
पवित्रमपि तत्क्षेत्रं नयन्ती सा पवित्रताम् .. 12 ..
5.24.m: from then on she is remembered in the world as the Gaṅgā Viṣṇupadī, / bringing that sacred field, although already holy, to [even greater] purity.

5.24.s:
evaṃ viṣṇoḥ padaṃ tatra saṃjātaṃ munisattamāḥ ..
sarvapāpaharaṃ puṃsāṃ tadā viṣṇupadī smṛtā .. 13 ..
5.24.d:
एवं विष्णोः पदं तत्र संजातं मुनिसत्तमाः ..
सर्वपापहरं पुंसां तदा विष्णुपदी स्मृता .. 13 ..
5.24.m: Thus Viṣṇu's footprint came to be there, O best of sages, / destroying all sins of men; then she was called Viṣṇupadī.

5.24.s:
yastasyāṃ śraddhayā yuktaḥ snānaṃ kṛtvā yathoditam ..
sparśayettatpadaṃ viṣṇoḥ sa yāti paramaṃ padam .. 14 ..
5.24.d:
यस्तस्यां श्रद्धया युक्तः स्नानं कृत्वा यथोदितम् ..
स्पर्शयेत्तत्पदं विष्णोः स याति परमं पदम् .. 14 ..
5.24.m: Whoever, endowed with faith, performs a ritual ablution in it as prescribed / and touches that footprint of Viṣṇu, goes to the supreme abode.

5.24.s:
yastatrakurute śrāddhaṃ samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ ..
snātvā viṣṇupadītoye gayāśrāddhaphalaṃ labhet .. 15 ..
5.24.d:
यस्तत्रकुरुते श्राद्धं सम्यक्छ्रद्धासमन्वितः ..
स्नात्वा विष्णुपदीतोये गयाश्राद्धफलं लभेत् .. 15 ..
5.24.m: Whoever performs a śrāddha there, fully endowed with faith, / having bathed in the water of Viṣṇupadī, obtains the fruit of a śrāddha at Gayā.

5.24.s:
māghamāse naraḥ snānaṃ prātarutthāya tatra yaḥ ..
karoti satataṃ martyaḥ sa prayāgaphalaṃ labhet .. 16 ..
5.24.d:
माघमासे नरः स्नानं प्रातरुत्थाय तत्र यः ..
करोति सततं मर्त्यः स प्रयागफलं लभेत् .. 16 ..
5.24.m: A mortal man who, having risen early in the month of Māgha, / constantly takes a ritual ablution there, obtains the fruit of Prayāga.

5.24.s:
athavā vatsaraṃ yāvatkṣaṇaṃ kṛtvātra bhaktitaḥ ..
tatra snānaṃ ca yaḥ kuryātsa muktiṃ labhate naraḥ .. 17 ..
5.24.d:
अथवा वत्सरं यावत्क्षणं कृत्वात्र भक्तितः ..
तत्र स्नानं च यः कुर्यात्स मुक्तिं लभते नरः .. 17 ..
5.24.m: Or whatever man takes leisure here for a year out of devotion / and performs a ritual ablution there, attains liberation.

5.24.s:
yasyāsthīni jale tatra kṣipyaṃte manujasya ca ..
api pāpa samācāraḥ sa prāpnoti parāṃ gatim .. 18 ..
5.24.d:
यस्यास्थीनि जले तत्र क्षिप्यंते मनुजस्य च ..
अपि पाप समाचारः स प्राप्नोति परां गतिम् .. 18 ..
5.24.m: The man whose bones are cast into that water, / even if of sinful conduct, attains the supreme path.

5.24.s:
api pakṣipataṃgā ye paśavaḥ kṛmayo mṛgāḥ ..
praviṣṭāḥ salile tasmiṃstṛṣārtā bhaktivarjitāḥ .. 19 ..
5.24.d:
अपि पक्षिपतंगा ये पशवः कृमयो मृगाः ..
प्रविष्टाः सलिले तस्मिंस्तृषार्ता भक्तिवर्जिताः .. 19 ..
5.24.m: Even birds, moths, cattle, worms, and wild animals / that have entered that water afflicted by thirst, devoid of devotion,

5.24.s:
te'pi pāpavinirmuktā dehāṃte cātidurlabham ..
cakriṇastatpadaṃ yāṃti jarāmaraṇavarjitam .. 6.24.20 ..
5.24.d:
तेऽपि पापविनिर्मुक्ता देहांते चातिदुर्लभम् ..
चक्रिणस्तत्पदं यांति जरामरणवर्जितम् .. 6.24.20 ..
5.24.m: even they, freed from sin at the end of their bodies, go to the very difficult to attain / abode of the discus-bearer, which is free from old age and death.

5.24.s:
kiṃ punaḥ śraddhayopetāḥ parvakāla upasthite ..
dattvā dānaṃ dvijendrāṇāṃ narā vedavidāṃ dvijāḥ .. 21 ..
5.24.d:
किं पुनः श्रद्धयोपेताः पर्वकाल उपस्थिते ..
दत्त्वा दानं द्विजेन्द्राणां नरा वेदविदां द्विजाः .. 21 ..
5.24.m: What then of men endowed with faith who, when a sacred occasion has arrived, / give gifts to the best of twice-born, the brahmins who know the Vedas, O twice-born?

5.24.s:
tatra gāthā purā gītā nāradena maharṣiṇā ..
viṣṇupadyāḥ samālokya prabhāvaṃ pāpanāśanam .. 22 ..
5.24.d:
तत्र गाथा पुरा गीता नारदेन महर्षिणा ..
विष्णुपद्याः समालोक्य प्रभावं पापनाशनम् .. 22 ..
5.24.m: Regarding this, a verse was sung long ago by the great seer Nārada, / having observed the sin-destroying power of Viṣṇupadī:

5.24.s:
kiṃ vratairniyamairvāpi tapobhirvividhairmakhaiḥ ..
kṛtairviṣṇupadītoye saṃsthite dharaṇītale .. 23 ..
5.24.d:
किं व्रतैर्नियमैर्वापि तपोभिर्विविधैर्मखैः ..
कृतैर्विष्णुपदीतोये संस्थिते धरणीतले .. 23 ..
5.24.m: "What [need is there] of vows, observances, diverse austerities, or sacrifices / performed, when the water of the Viṣṇupadī is present on the surface of the earth?

5.24.s:
ekaḥ sarveṣu tīrtheṣu snānaṃ martyaḥ samācaret ..
eko viṣṇupadītoye snāti dvābhyāṃ samaṃ phalam .. 24 ..
5.24.d:
एकः सर्वेषु तीर्थेषु स्नानं मर्त्यः समाचरेत् ..
एको विष्णुपदीतोये स्नाति द्वाभ्यां समं फलम् .. 24 ..
5.24.m: One mortal may perform a ritual ablution at all sacred fords; / one bathes in the water of Viṣṇupadī: for both, the fruit is equal.

5.24.s:
eko dānāni sarvāṇi brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayacchati ..
eko viṣṇupadītoye snāti dvābhyāṃ samaṃ hi tat .. 25 ..
5.24.d:
एको दानानि सर्वाणि ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रयच्छति ..
एको विष्णुपदीतोये स्नाति द्वाभ्यां समं हि तत् .. 25 ..
5.24.m: One gives all gifts to brahmins; / one bathes in the water of Viṣṇupadī: that indeed is equal for both.

5.24.s:
pañcāgnisādhako grīṣme varṣāsvākāśamāśritaḥ ..
jalāśrayaśca hemaṃta ekaḥ syātpuruṣaḥ kṣitau .. 26 ..
5.24.d:
पञ्चाग्निसाधको ग्रीष्मे वर्षास्वाकाशमाश्रितः ..
जलाश्रयश्च हेमंत एकः स्यात्पुरुषः क्षितौ .. 26 ..
5.24.m: One man on earth may practice the five fires in summer, / dwell in the open air in the rains, and stay in water in winter;

5.24.s:
anyo viṣṇupadītoye snātvā viṣṇupadaṃ spṛśet ..
tāvubhāvapi nirdiṣṭau samau puruṣasattamau .. 27 ..
5.24.d:
अन्यो विष्णुपदीतोये स्नात्वा विष्णुपदं स्पृशेत् ..
तावुभावपि निर्दिष्टौ समौ पुरुषसत्तमौ .. 27 ..
5.24.m: another, having bathed in the water of Viṣṇupadī, touches the footprint of Viṣṇu: / both of those best among men are declared to be equal.

5.24.s:
ekāṃtaropavāsī ya ekaḥ syājjīvitāvadhi ..
ekoviṣṇupadītoye snāti dvābhyāṃ samaṃ phalam .. 28 ..
5.24.d:
एकांतरोपवासी य एकः स्याज्जीवितावधि ..
एकोविष्णुपदीतोये स्नाति द्वाभ्यां समं फलम् .. 28 ..
5.24.m: One may fast on alternate days until the end of his life; / one bathes in the water of Viṣṇupadī: the fruit is equal for both.

5.24.s:
trirātropoṣitastveko yāvadvarṣaśataṃ naraḥ ..
eko viṣṇupadītoye snāti dvābhyāṃ samaṃ phalam .. 29 ..
5.24.d:
त्रिरात्रोपोषितस्त्वेको यावद्वर्षशतं नरः ..
एको विष्णुपदीतोये स्नाति द्वाभ्यां समं फलम् .. 29 ..
5.24.m: One man fasts for three nights [at a time] for a hundred years; / one bathes in the water of Viṣṇupadī: the fruit is equal for both."

5.24.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evamuktvā muniśreṣṭho nārado dvijasattamāḥ ..
virarāma munīnāṃ sa bahūnāṃ purato'sakṛt .. 6.24.30 ..
5.24.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्वा मुनिश्रेष्ठो नारदो द्विजसत्तमाः ..
विरराम मुनीनां स बहूनां पुरतोऽसकृत् .. 6.24.30 ..
5.24.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, O best of twice-born, the best of sages, Nārada, / ceased speaking in the presence of many sages repeatedly.

5.24.s:
tasmātsarva prayatnena snānaṃ tatra samācareta ..
saṃspṛśecca padaṃ viṣṇorya icchecchreya ātmanaḥ .. 31 ..
5.24.d:
तस्मात्सर्व प्रयत्नेन स्नानं तत्र समाचरेत ..
संस्पृशेच्च पदं विष्णोर्य इच्छेच्छ्रेय आत्मनः .. 31 ..
5.24.m: Therefore, whoever desires his own welfare should with all effort / perform a ritual ablution there and touch the footprint of Viṣṇu.

5.24.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
yadetadbhavatā proktamātmānaṃ vinivedayet ..
viṣṇoḥ padasya saṃprāpte ayane dakṣiṇottare .. 32 ..
5.24.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
यदेतद्भवता प्रोक्तमात्मानं विनिवेदयेत् ..
विष्णोः पदस्य संप्राप्ते अयने दक्षिणोत्तरे .. 32 ..
5.24.m: The seers said: / As to what was stated by you, that one should dedicate oneself / at the footprint of Viṣṇu when the southern and northern solstices arrive,

5.24.s:
tatkena vidhinā sūta mantraiśca vada satvaram ..
vayaṃ yena ca tatkurmaḥ sarvaṃ bhaktisamanvitāḥ .. 33 ..
5.24.d:
तत्केन विधिना सूत मन्त्रैश्च वद सत्वरम् ..
वयं येन च तत्कुर्मः सर्वं भक्तिसमन्विताः .. 33 ..
5.24.m: tell [us] quickly, O Sūta, by what rite and with which mantras, / so that we may do all that endowed with devotion.

5.24.s:
.. sūta uvāca ..
dakṣiṇe cottare cāpi saṃprāpte cāyanadvaye ..
pūjayitvā padaṃ viṣṇorimaṃ mantramudīrayet .. 34 ..
5.24.d:
.. सूत उवाच ..
दक्षिणे चोत्तरे चापि संप्राप्ते चायनद्वये ..
पूजयित्वा पदं विष्णोरिमं मन्त्रमुदीरयेत् .. 34 ..
5.24.m: Sūta said: / When both the southern and northern solstices arrive, / having worshipped the footprint of Viṣṇu, one should recite this mantra:

5.24.s:
ṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtare mṛtyuryadyakasmādbhavenmama ..
tatte padaṃ gatirme syādahaṃ te bhṛtyatāṃ gataḥ .. 35 ..
5.24.d:
षण्मासाभ्यंतरे मृत्युर्यद्यकस्माद्भवेन्मम ..
तत्ते पदं गतिर्मे स्यादहं ते भृत्यतां गतः .. 35 ..
5.24.m: "If my death should suddenly occur within six months, / let that footprint of yours be my goal; I have become your servant."

5.24.s:
evaṃ procya hariṃ paścātpūjayedbrāhmaṇāṃstataḥ ..
atha taiḥ samamaśnīyāttataḥ prāpnoti sadgatim .. 36 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye viṣṇupadītīrthotpattivarṇanaṃnāma caturviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 24 .. ..
5.24.d:
एवं प्रोच्य हरिं पश्चात्पूजयेद्ब्राह्मणांस्ततः ..
अथ तैः सममश्नीयात्ततः प्राप्नोति सद्गतिम् .. 36 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये विष्णुपदीतीर्थोत्पत्तिवर्णनंनाम चतुर्विंशोऽध्यायः .. 24 .. ..
5.24.m:
Having spoken thus to Hari, he should afterwards worship the brahmins; / then he should eat together with them; thereafter he attains the auspicious path.
Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, named 'Description of the Origin of the Viṣṇupadī Sacred Ford' in the Praise of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa in eighty-one thousand verses.

5.25.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tatrāścaryamabhūtpūrvaṃ yattadbrāhmaṇasattamāḥ ..
tadvo'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi gaṃgāmāhātmyasaṃbhavam .. 1 ..
5.25.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तत्राश्चर्यमभूत्पूर्वं यत्तद्ब्राह्मणसत्तमाः ..
तद्वोऽहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि गंगामाहात्म्यसंभवम् .. 1 ..
5.25.m: Sūta said: / A wonder took place there in the past, O best of brahmins; / I shall recount that to you, arising from the greatness of the Gaṅgā.

5.25.s:
camatkārapure vipraḥ purāsītsaṃśitavrataḥ ..
caṃḍaśarmeti vikhyāto rūpaudāryaguṇānvitaḥ .. 2 ..
5.25.d:
चमत्कारपुरे विप्रः पुरासीत्संशितव्रतः ..
चंडशर्मेति विख्यातो रूपौदार्यगुणान्वितः .. 2 ..
5.25.m: In the city of Camatkārapura, there was formerly a brahmin of strict vows, / known as Caṇḍaśarman, endowed with beauty, generosity, and virtues.

5.25.s:
sa yadā yauvanopetastadā veśyānurāgakṛt ..
śrotriyo'pyabhavadvipro yauvanodbhārapīḍitaḥ .. 3 ..
5.25.d:
स यदा यौवनोपेतस्तदा वेश्यानुरागकृत् ..
श्रोत्रियोऽप्यभवद्विप्रो यौवनोद्भारपीडितः .. 3 ..
5.25.m: When he was endowed with youth, he developed a passion for a courtesan; / though a Vedic scholar, the brahmin became afflicted by the heavy burden of youth.

5.25.s:
sa kadācinniśīthe'tha tṛṣārtaśca samutthitaḥ ..
prārthayāmāsa tāṃ veśyāṃ pānīyaṃ pātumutsahe .. 4 ..
5.25.d:
स कदाचिन्निशीथेऽथ तृषार्तश्च समुत्थितः ..
प्रार्थयामास तां वेश्यां पानीयं पातुमुत्सहे .. 4 ..
5.25.m: Once, getting up at midnight afflicted by thirst, / he begged that courtesan: "I wish to drink water."

5.25.s:
atha sā salilabhrāṃtyā karakaṃ madyasaṃbhavam ..
samādāya dadau pānaṃ tasmai nidrākulāya ca .. 5 ..
5.25.d:
अथ सा सलिलभ्रांत्या करकं मद्यसंभवम् ..
समादाय ददौ पानं तस्मै निद्राकुलाय च .. 5 ..
5.25.m: Then she, mistaking it for water, took a water-pot containing liquor / and gave the drink to him, who was overcome by sleep.

5.25.s:
mukhamadhyagate madye so'pi tāṃ kopasaṃyutaḥ..
veśyāṃ prabhartsayāmāsa dhigdhikśabdairmuhurmuhuḥ ..6..
5.25.d:
मुखमध्यगते मद्ये सोऽपि तां कोपसंयुतः..
वेश्यां प्रभर्त्सयामास धिग्धिक्शब्दैर्मुहुर्मुहुः ..6..
5.25.m: When the liquor entered his mouth, he, filled with rage, / reproached the courtesan with the repeated words: "Fie! Fie!"

5.25.s:
kimidaṃkimidaṃ pāpe tvayā karma vigarhitam ..
kṛtaṃ yanmukhamadhye me prakṣiptā niṃditā surā .. 7 ..
5.25.d:
किमिदंकिमिदं पापे त्वया कर्म विगर्हितम् ..
कृतं यन्मुखमध्ये मे प्रक्षिप्ता निंदिता सुरा .. 7 ..
5.25.m: "What is this, what is this, O sinful woman! A vile deed has been done / by you, in that despicable liquor has been poured into my mouth!

5.25.s:
brāhmaṇyamadya me naṣṭaṃ madyapānādasaṃśayam ..
prāyaścittaṃ kariṣyāmi tasmādātmaviśuddhaye .. 8 ..
5.25.d:
ब्राह्मण्यमद्य मे नष्टं मद्यपानादसंशयम् ..
प्रायश्चित्तं करिष्यामि तस्मादात्मविशुद्धये .. 8 ..
5.25.m: My brahminhood is destroyed today through drinking liquor, without doubt; / therefore, I shall perform an expiation for the purification of myself."

5.25.s:
evamuktvā viniṣkramya tadgṛhādduḥkhasaṃyutaḥ ..
rurodātha tadā gatvā karuṇaṃ nirjane vane .. 9 ..
5.25.d:
एवमुक्त्वा विनिष्क्रम्य तद्गृहाद्दुःखसंयुतः ..
रुरोदाथ तदा गत्वा करुणं निर्जने वने .. 9 ..
5.25.m: Having spoken thus, having gone out from her house filled with sorrow, / he then went to a lonely forest and wept piteously.

5.25.s:
tataḥ prabhātavelāyāṃ snātvā vastrasamanvitaḥ ..
tyaktvā gātrasya romāṇi samastāni dvijottamāḥ .. 6.25.10 ..
5.25.d:
ततः प्रभातवेलायां स्नात्वा वस्त्रसमन्वितः ..
त्यक्त्वा गात्रस्य रोमाणि समस्तानि द्विजोत्तमाः .. 6.25.10 ..
5.25.m: Then at daybreak, having bathed, wearing [clean] clothes, / having shaved all the hair of his body, O best of twice-born,

5.25.s:
saṃprāpto vipramukhyānāṃ sabhā yatra vyavasthitā ..
paṭhaṃti sarvaśāstrāṇi vedāṃtāni ca kṛtsnaśaḥ .. 11 ..
5.25.d:
संप्राप्तो विप्रमुख्यानां सभा यत्र व्यवस्थिता ..
पठंति सर्वशास्त्राणि वेदांतानि च कृत्स्नशः .. 11 ..
5.25.m: He arrived where the assembly of leading brahmins was seated, / reading all the scriptures and the entirety of the Upaniṣads.

5.25.s:
athāsau praṇipatyoccaiḥ provāca dvijasattamān..
jalabhrāṃtyā surā pītā mayā kuruta nigraham .. 12 ..
5.25.d:
अथासौ प्रणिपत्योच्चैः प्रोवाच द्विजसत्तमान्..
जलभ्रांत्या सुरा पीता मया कुरुत निग्रहम् .. 12 ..
5.25.m: Then, prostrating himself, he said loudly to the best of brahmins: / “Mistaking it for water, I drank wine; punish me!”

5.25.s:
atha te dharmaśāstrāṇi pravicārya punaḥpunaḥ ..
tamūcurbrāhmaṇāḥ sarve prāyaścittakṛte sthitam.. 13 ..
5.25.d:
अथ ते धर्मशास्त्राणि प्रविचार्य पुनःपुनः ..
तमूचुर्ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे प्रायश्चित्तकृते स्थितम्.. 13 ..
5.25.m: Then all those brahmins, deliberating again and again over the Dharmaśāstras, / said to him as he stood ready for penance:

5.25.s:
.. brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ ..
ajñānājjñānato vāpi surāṃ cedbrāhmaṇaḥ pibet..
agnivarṇaṃ ghṛtaṃ pītvā tāvanmātraṃviśu dhyati .. 14 ..
5.25.d:
.. ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः ..
अज्ञानाज्ज्ञानतो वापि सुरां चेद्ब्राह्मणः पिबेत्..
अग्निवर्णं घृतं पीत्वा तावन्मात्रंविशु ध्यति .. 14 ..
5.25.m: The brahmins said: / “If a brahmin drinks wine, whether unknowingly or knowingly, / he is purified only by drinking that same amount of fire-hot ghee.

5.25.s:
sa tvaṃ vāṃchasi cecchuddhimagnivarṇaṃ ghṛtaṃ piba ..
yāvanmātrā surā pītā tāvanmātraṃ viśuddhaye .. 15 ..
5.25.d:
स त्वं वांछसि चेच्छुद्धिमग्निवर्णं घृतं पिब ..
यावन्मात्रा सुरा पीता तावन्मात्रं विशुद्धये .. 15 ..
5.25.m: So, if you desire purification, drink fire-hot ghee; / for purification, drink only as much wine as you have drunk.”

5.25.s:
sa tatheti pratijñāya ghṛtamādāya tatkṣaṇāt ..
cakre vahnisamaṃ yāvatpānārthaṃ dvijasattamāḥ.. 16 ..
5.25.d:
स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय घृतमादाय तत्क्षणात् ..
चक्रे वह्निसमं यावत्पानार्थं द्विजसत्तमाः.. 16 ..
5.25.m: Agreeing, “So be it,” and taking the ghee at that very moment, / O best of brahmins, just as he made it blazing like fire to drink,

5.25.s:
tāvattasya pitā prāptaḥ śrutvā vārtāṃ sabhāryakaḥ ..
kimidaṃ kimidaṃ putra bruvāṇo duḥkha saṃyutaḥ ..
aśrupūrṇekṣaṇo dīno vāṣpagadgadayā girā .. 17 ..
tataḥ sa kathayāmāsa sarvarātrisamudbhavam..
vṛttāṃtaṃ tacca viprāṇāṃ prāyaścittaṃ yathocitam .. ...8..
atha sa brāhmaṇānprāha sarvāṃstāndvijasattamāḥ ..
prāyaścittaṃ sutāyāsmai mamānyatsaṃpradīyatām ...9..
5.25.d:
तावत्तस्य पिता प्राप्तः श्रुत्वा वार्तां सभार्यकः ..
किमिदं किमिदं पुत्र ब्रुवाणो दुःख संयुतः ..
अश्रुपूर्णेक्षणो दीनो वाष्पगद्गदया गिरा .. 17 ..
ततः स कथयामास सर्वरात्रिसमुद्भवम्..
वृत्तांतं तच्च विप्राणां प्रायश्चित्तं यथोचितम् .. ...8..
अथ स ब्राह्मणान्प्राह सर्वांस्तान्द्विजसत्तमाः ..
प्रायश्चित्तं सुतायास्मै ममान्यत्संप्रदीयताम् ...9..
5.25.m:
his father, accompanied by his wife, arrived upon hearing the news, / saying, “What is this? What is this, son?”, filled with sorrow, / distressed, his eyes full of tears, his voice choked with weeping.
Then he recounted the entire event that had occurred in the night / and that appropriate penance prescribed by the brahmins.
Then he said to all those brahmins, O best of brahmins: / “Let another penance be prescribed for this son of mine!

5.25.s:
saṃcintya dharmaśāstrāṇi vicārya ca punaḥ punaḥ ..
sarvasvamapi dāsyāmi putrahetorasaṃśayam .. 6.25.20 ..
tataste brāhmaṇāḥ sarve bhūyobhūyaśca sādaram ..
viciṃtya dharmaśāstrāṇi tamūcurmunisattamāḥ .. ..2...
5.25.d:
संचिन्त्य धर्मशास्त्राणि विचार्य च पुनः पुनः ..
सर्वस्वमपि दास्यामि पुत्रहेतोरसंशयम् .. 6.25.20 ..
ततस्ते ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे भूयोभूयश्च सादरम् ..
विचिंत्य धर्मशास्त्राणि तमूचुर्मुनिसत्तमाः .. ..2...
5.25.m:
Having reflected on the Dharmaśāstras and deliberated again and again, / I will undoubtedly give away even my entire property for the sake of my son.”
Then all those brahmins, having reflected on the Dharmaśāstras / respectfully again and again, said to him, O best of sages:

5.25.s:
nānyadasti surāpāne prāyaścittaṃ dvijanmanām ..
mauṃjīhomaṃ vinā vipra yadyuktaṃ tatsamācara ..22..
5.25.d:
नान्यदस्ति सुरापाने प्रायश्चित्तं द्विजन्मनाम् ..
मौंजीहोमं विना विप्र यद्युक्तं तत्समाचर ..22..
5.25.m: “There is no other penance for the twice-born in the drinking of wine / except the burning on the muñja-grass pyre, O brahmin; carry out what is prescribed.”

5.25.s:
tataḥ sa svasutaṃ prāha naiva tvaṃ kartumarhasi ..
yaccha dānāni viprebhyastīrthayātrāṃ samācara .. 23 ..
5.25.d:
ततः स स्वसुतं प्राह नैव त्वं कर्तुमर्हसि ..
यच्छ दानानि विप्रेभ्यस्तीर्थयात्रां समाचर .. 23 ..
5.25.m: Then he said to his son: “You must not do this at all; / give gifts to the brahmins and undertake a pilgrimage to sacred fords.

5.25.s:
tataḥ śuddhiṃ samāpnoṣi kramānniyamasaṃyutaḥ ..
vrataiśca vividhaiścīrṇaiḥ satyametadbravīmyaham .. 24 ..
5.25.d:
ततः शुद्धिं समाप्नोषि क्रमान्नियमसंयुतः ..
व्रतैश्च विविधैश्चीर्णैः सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीम्यहम् .. 24 ..
5.25.m: Then you will gradually attain purity, observing vows / and having performed various religious observances; this I speak truthfully.”

5.25.s: na brāhmaṇasamādiṣṭaṃ prāyaścitta viśuddhaye .. 25 ..
5.25.d: न ब्राह्मणसमादिष्टं प्रायश्चित्त विशुद्धये .. 25 ..
5.25.m: “The penance prescribed by the brahmins is not for purification.”

5.25.s:
.. putra uvāca .. ..
etanmama mahābhāgā yadbruvaṃti vratādikam ..
tasmātkāryo mayā tāta mauṃjīhomo na saṃśayaḥ .. 26 ..
5.25.d:
.. पुत्र उवाच .. ..
एतन्मम महाभागा यद्ब्रुवंति व्रतादिकम् ..
तस्मात्कार्यो मया तात मौंजीहोमो न संशयः .. 26 ..
5.25.m: The son said: / “Since these noble souls prescribe this, such as vows, / therefore, father, the burning on the muñja-grass pyre must undoubtedly be performed by me.

5.25.s: yanmayā tu kṛtaṃ bālye tatsarvaṃ kṣaṃtumarhasi .. 27 ..
5.25.d: यन्मया तु कृतं बाल्ये तत्सर्वं क्षंतुमर्हसि .. 27 ..
5.25.m: You ought to forgive all that I have done in childhood.”

5.25.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tasya taṃ niścayaṃ jñātvā sa pitā sutavatsalaḥ ..
sarvasvaṃ pradadau ruṣṭo maraṇe kṛtaniścayaḥ .. 28 ..
5.25.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तस्य तं निश्चयं ज्ञात्वा स पिता सुतवत्सलः ..
सर्वस्वं प्रददौ रुष्टो मरणे कृतनिश्चयः .. 28 ..
5.25.m: Sūta said: / Knowing his resolve, that father, loving towards his son, / gave away all his possessions in grief, resolved upon death.

5.25.s:
sā'pi tasya satī bhāryā kṛtvā mṛtyuviniścayam ..
tamuvāca sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvaṃ dattvā gṛhādikam.. 29 ..
5.25.d:
साऽपि तस्य सती भार्या कृत्वा मृत्युविनिश्चयम् ..
तमुवाच सुतं दृष्ट्वा सर्वं दत्त्वा गृहादिकम्.. 29 ..
5.25.m: His devoted wife also, having resolved upon death, / looked at her son after giving away everything, including their house, and said to him:

5.25.s:
āvābhyāṃ saṃpraviṣṭābhyāṃ vahnau putra tatastadā ..
mauṃjīhomastvayā kāryo māṃ tātaṃ yadi manyase .. 6.25.30 ..
5.25.d:
आवाभ्यां संप्रविष्टाभ्यां वह्नौ पुत्र ततस्तदा ..
मौंजीहोमस्त्वया कार्यो मां तातं यदि मन्यसे .. 6.25.30 ..
5.25.m: “Only when the two of us have entered the fire, son, / is the burning on the muñja-grass pyre to be done by you, if you regard me and your father.”

5.25.s:
tatastau dampatī hṛṣṭau yāvadvahnisamīpagau ..
saṃjātau maraṇārthāya sa ca tābhyāṃ samudbhavaḥ .. 31 ..
5.25.d:
ततस्तौ दम्पती हृष्टौ यावद्वह्निसमीपगौ ..
संजातौ मरणार्थाय स च ताभ्यां समुद्भवः .. 31 ..
5.25.m: Then, as the married couple cheerfully approached the fire / to die, and the son born of the two of them [did likewise],

5.25.s:
tāvatprāpto munirnāma śāṃḍilyo vedapāragaḥ ..
tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena tatra deśe dvijottamāḥ .. 32 ..
5.25.d:
तावत्प्राप्तो मुनिर्नाम शांडिल्यो वेदपारगः ..
तीर्थयात्राप्रसंगेन तत्र देशे द्विजोत्तमाः .. 32 ..
5.25.m: just then a sage named Śāṇḍilya, master of the Vedas, / arrived in that region, O best of brahmins, in the course of a pilgrimage to sacred fords.

5.25.s:
sa vṛttāṃtaṃ samākarṇya kopasaṃraktalocanaḥ ..
abravīdbrāhmaṇānsarvānbhartsamāno muhurmuhuḥ .. 33 ..
5.25.d:
स वृत्तांतं समाकर्ण्य कोपसंरक्तलोचनः ..
अब्रवीद्ब्राह्मणान्सर्वान्भर्त्समानो मुहुर्मुहुः .. 33 ..
5.25.m: Having heard the incident, his eyes red with anger, / he spoke to all the brahmins, censuring them repeatedly:

5.25.s:
aho mūḍhatamā yūyaṃ yadetadbrāhmaṇatrayam ..
vṛthā mṛtyumavāpnoti nigrahe sugame sati..34..
5.25.d:
अहो मूढतमा यूयं यदेतद्ब्राह्मणत्रयम् ..
वृथा मृत्युमवाप्नोति निग्रहे सुगमे सति..34..
5.25.m: “Ah, you are utter fools, since this trio of brahmins / meets death in vain when an easy expiation exists!

5.25.s:
atra kātyāyanenoktaṃ yadvacaḥ sumahātmanā ..
tacchṛṇvantu dvijāḥ sarve prāyaścittī tathāpyayam .. 35 ..
5.25.d:
अत्र कात्यायनेनोक्तं यद्वचः सुमहात्मना ..
तच्छृण्वन्तु द्विजाः सर्वे प्रायश्चित्ती तथाप्ययम् .. 35 ..
5.25.m: Let all the brahmins hear the word spoken here by the great-souled Kātyāyana, / and likewise he who requires penance:

5.25.s:
cāṃdrāyaṇāni kṛcchrāṇi tathā sāṃtapanāni ca ..
prāyaścittāni dīyaṃte yatra gaṃgā na vidyate .. 36 ..
5.25.d:
चांद्रायणानि कृच्छ्राणि तथा सांतपनानि च ..
प्रायश्चित्तानि दीयंते यत्र गंगा न विद्यते .. 36 ..
5.25.m: ‘Cāndrāyaṇas, kṛcchras, and sāṃtapanas— / such penances are prescribed only where the Gaṅgā does not exist.’

5.25.s:
atra viṣṇupadī gaṃgā tatkṣetre tu dvijottamāḥ ..
tasyāṃ snānaṃ karotveṣa tataḥ śuddhimavāpsyati .. 37 ..
5.25.d:
अत्र विष्णुपदी गंगा तत्क्षेत्रे तु द्विजोत्तमाः ..
तस्यां स्नानं करोत्वेष ततः शुद्धिमवाप्स्यति .. 37 ..
5.25.m: Here in this sacred field is the Gaṅgā, the Viṣṇupadī, O best of brahmins; / let him bathe in it, and then he will attain purification.

5.25.s:
mauṃjīhomaḥ pramāṇaṃ syānmunivākyena cedbhavet ..
tadetadapi vākyaṃ hi kātyāyanamuneḥ sphuṭam .. 38 ..
5.25.d:
मौंजीहोमः प्रमाणं स्यान्मुनिवाक्येन चेद्भवेत् ..
तदेतदपि वाक्यं हि कात्यायनमुनेः स्फुटम् .. 38 ..
5.25.m: The burning on the muñja-grass pyre would be valid if it were the word of a sage; / and this statement here is indeed clearly that of the sage Kātyāyana.”

5.25.s:
tataste brāhmaṇāḥ sarve harṣeṇa mahatānvitāḥ ..
sādhusādhviti taṃ procya procuḥ satyamidaṃ mune .. 39 ..
5.25.d:
ततस्ते ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे हर्षेण महतान्विताः ..
साधुसाध्विति तं प्रोच्य प्रोचुः सत्यमिदं मुने .. 39 ..
5.25.m: Then all those brahmins, filled with great joy, / exclaimed to him, “Excellent! Excellent!”, and said: “This is true, O sage!”

5.25.s:
tataḥ prabodhya taṃ vipraṃ ninyustatra dvijottamāḥ ..
yatra viṣṇupadī gaṃgā svayameva vyavasthitā .. 6.25.40 ..
5.25.d:
ततः प्रबोध्य तं विप्रं निन्युस्तत्र द्विजोत्तमाः ..
यत्र विष्णुपदी गंगा स्वयमेव व्यवस्थिता .. 6.25.40 ..
5.25.m: Then, consoling that brahmin, the best of the twice-born led him there / where the Viṣṇupadī Gaṅgā herself was present.

5.25.s:
tatra sa brāhmaṇo yāvadgaṃgātoyasamudbhavam ..
gaṃḍūṣaṃ kurute vaktre tāvacchuddho babhūva saḥ ..
udarādakhilaṃ toyaṃ niṣkrāṃtaṃ dvijasattamāḥ .. 41 ..
5.25.d:
तत्र स ब्राह्मणो यावद्गंगातोयसमुद्भवम् ..
गंडूषं कुरुते वक्त्रे तावच्छुद्धो बभूव सः ..
उदरादखिलं तोयं निष्क्रांतं द्विजसत्तमाः .. 41 ..
5.25.m: There, as soon as that brahmin took a mouthful / of the water from the Gaṅgā into his mouth, he became purified; / all the water [he had drunk] came out of his belly, O best of brahmins.

5.25.s:
tato'vagāhate yāvattasyāstoyaṃ suśobhanam ..
tāvadākāśasaṃbhūtā gambhīrovāca bhāratī .. 42 ..
5.25.d:
ततोऽवगाहते यावत्तस्यास्तोयं सुशोभनम् ..
तावदाकाशसंभूता गम्भीरोवाच भारती .. 42 ..
5.25.m: Then, as he plunged into its beautiful water, / a deep voice born of the sky spoke:

5.25.s:
śuddho'yaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ sākṣādviṣṇupadyāḥ samāgamāt ..
snānādācamanādeva tasmādyātu gṛhaṃ nijam .. .. 43 ..
5.25.d:
शुद्धोऽयं ब्राह्मणः साक्षाद्विष्णुपद्याः समागमात् ..
स्नानादाचमनादेव तस्माद्यातु गृहं निजम् .. .. 43 ..
5.25.m: “This brahmin is purified directly by the contact with the Viṣṇupadī, / merely by bathing and sipping its water; therefore, let him go to his own home.”

5.25.s:
tataste brāhmaṇāḥ sarve caṃḍaśarmādayaśca ye ..
diṣṭyādiṣṭyeti jalpantaḥ svāni harmyāṇi bhejire .. 44 ..
5.25.d:
ततस्ते ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे चंडशर्मादयश्च ये ..
दिष्ट्यादिष्ट्येति जल्पन्तः स्वानि हर्म्याणि भेजिरे .. 44 ..
5.25.m: Then all those brahmins, Caṇḍaśarman and the others, / saying, “By good fortune! By good fortune!”, went to their own mansions.

5.25.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ prabhāvā sā viprā gaṃgā viṣṇupadī sthitā ..
tasya kṣetrasya sīmāṃte paścime pāpanāśinī .. 45 ..
5.25.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं प्रभावा सा विप्रा गंगा विष्णुपदी स्थिता ..
तस्य क्षेत्रस्य सीमांते पश्चिमे पापनाशिनी .. 45 ..
5.25.m: Sūta said: / Such is the power of the Gaṅgā Viṣṇupadī, O brahmins, / situated at the western border of that sacred field, destroying sin.

5.25.s:
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ viṣṇupadyāḥ samudbhavam ..
māhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvapātakanāśanam .. 46 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvara kṣetramāhātmye viṣṇupadīgaṃgāmāhāmyavarṇanaṃnāma pañcaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 25 .. .. cha ..
5.25.d:
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं विष्णुपद्याः समुद्भवम् ..
माहात्म्यं ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठाः सर्वपातकनाशनम् .. 46 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वर क्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये विष्णुपदीगंगामाहाम्यवर्णनंनाम पञ्चविंशोऽध्यायः .. 25 .. .. छ ..
5.25.m:
All this has been related to you: the origin of the Viṣṇupadī, / a māhātmya that destroys all evils, O best of brahmins.
Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, named ‘Description of the Māhātmya of the Viṣṇupadī Gaṅgā’, in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

5.26.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
yatpūrvāparasīmāntaṃ tanmayā saṃprakīrtitam ..
dakṣiṇottarasaṃbhūtaṃ tadvo vakṣyāmi sāṃpratam .. 1 ..
5.26.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
यत्पूर्वापरसीमान्तं तन्मया संप्रकीर्तितम् ..
दक्षिणोत्तरसंभूतं तद्वो वक्ष्यामि सांप्रतम् .. 1 ..
5.26.m: Sūta said: / The eastern and western borders have been fully proclaimed by me; / now I shall speak to you of that which belongs to the south and north.

5.26.s:
asti bhūbhitale khyātā madhurākhyā mahāpurī ..
nānāviprasamākīrṇā yamunātaṭasaṃśrayā .. 2 ..
5.26.d:
अस्ति भूभितले ख्याता मधुराख्या महापुरी ..
नानाविप्रसमाकीर्णा यमुनातटसंश्रया .. 2 ..
5.26.m: On the surface of the earth there is a celebrated great city named Madhurā, / crowded with various brahmins and situated on the bank of the Yamunā.

5.26.s:
tasyāmāsīddvijaśreṣṭho gokarṇa iti viśrutaḥ ..
vedādhyayanasaṃpannaḥ sarvaśāstravicakṣaṇaḥ .. 3 ..
5.26.d:
तस्यामासीद्द्विजश्रेष्ठो गोकर्ण इति विश्रुतः ..
वेदाध्ययनसंपन्नः सर्वशास्त्रविचक्षणः .. 3 ..
5.26.m: In it was an excellent twice-born known as Gokarṇa, / endowed with the study of the Vedas and skilled in all the scriptures.

5.26.s:
athāparo'sti tannāmā tatra vipro vayo'nvitaḥ ..
so'pi ca brāhmaṇaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvavidyāsu pāragaḥ .. 4 ..
5.26.d:
अथापरोऽस्ति तन्नामा तत्र विप्रो वयोऽन्वितः ..
सोऽपि च ब्राह्मणः श्रेष्ठः सर्वविद्यासु पारगः .. 4 ..
5.26.m: Now there was another aged brahmin of the same name there; / he too was an excellent brahmin, a master in all fields of knowledge.

5.26.s:
kasyacittvathakālasya yamaḥ prāha svakiṃkaram ..
ūrdhvakeśaṃ suraktākṣaṃ kṛṣṇadantaṃ bhayānakam .. 5 ..
5.26.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथकालस्य यमः प्राह स्वकिंकरम् ..
ऊर्ध्वकेशं सुरक्ताक्षं कृष्णदन्तं भयानकम् .. 5 ..
5.26.m: Then, after some time, Yama spoke to his servant, / who had hair standing upright, very red eyes, black teeth, and a terrifying appearance:

5.26.s:
adya gaccha drutaṃ dūta mathurākhyāṃ mahāpurīm ..
ānayasva dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ tasyāṃ gokarṇasaṃjñakam .. 6 ..
5.26.d:
अद्य गच्छ द्रुतं दूत मथुराख्यां महापुरीम् ..
आनयस्व द्विजश्रेष्ठं तस्यां गोकर्णसंज्ञकम् .. 6 ..
5.26.m: "Go quickly today, messenger, to the great city called Mathurā. / Bring from it the excellent twice-born named Gokarṇa.

5.26.s:
tasyāyuṣaḥ kṣayo jāto madhyāhne'dyatane dine ..
tyājyo'nyo'sti ca tatraiva cirāyustādṛśo dvijaḥ .. .7 ..
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
atha dūto drutaṃ gatvā tāṃ purīṃ yamaśāsanāt ..
vibhramādānayāmāsa gokarṇaṃ ca cirāyuṣam.. 8 ..
5.26.d:
तस्यायुषः क्षयो जातो मध्याह्नेऽद्यतने दिने ..
त्याज्योऽन्योऽस्ति च तत्रैव चिरायुस्तादृशो द्विजः .. .7 ..
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अथ दूतो द्रुतं गत्वा तां पुरीं यमशासनात् ..
विभ्रमादानयामास गोकर्णं च चिरायुषम्.. 8 ..
5.26.m:
The end of his lifespan has arrived at midday on this very day. / Another twice-born of that [same name] there is to be left alone, who is long-lived."
Sūta said:
Then, having gone quickly to that city by Yama's order, / out of confusion the messenger brought Gokarṇa, the one who was long-lived.

5.26.s:
tataḥ kopaparītātmā yamaḥ provāca kiṃkaram ..
dīrghāyureṣa ānīto dhikpāpa kimidaṃ kṛtam ..9..
5.26.d:
ततः कोपपरीतात्मा यमः प्रोवाच किंकरम् ..
दीर्घायुरेष आनीतो धिक्पाप किमिदं कृतम् ..9..
5.26.m: Then Yama, his mind filled with anger, spoke to the servant: / "This long-lived one has been brought! Curse you, sinner! What is this you have done?

5.26.s:
tasmātprāpaya tatraiva yāvadasya ca bandhubhiḥ ..
no gātraṃ dahyate śokātsusamiddhena vahninā .. 6.26.10 ..
5.26.d:
तस्मात्प्रापय तत्रैव यावदस्य च बन्धुभिः ..
नो गात्रं दह्यते शोकात्सुसमिद्धेन वह्निना .. 6.26.10 ..
5.26.m: Therefore return him to that very place, as long as by his kinsmen / his body is not burned out of grief by a fully kindled fire."

5.26.s:
.. .. brāhmaṇa uvāca .. ..
nāhaṃ tatra gamiṣyāmi diṣṭyā prāptosmi teṃ'tikam..
vāṃchamānaḥ sadā mṛtyuṃ dāridryeṇa kadarthitaḥ .. 11 ..
5.26.d:
.. .. ब्राह्मण उवाच .. ..
नाहं तत्र गमिष्यामि दिष्ट्या प्राप्तोस्मि तेंऽतिकम्..
वांछमानः सदा मृत्युं दारिद्र्येण कदर्थितः .. 11 ..
5.26.m:
The brahmin said:
"I will not go there; by good fortune I have reached your presence, / desiring death at all times, tormented by poverty."

5.26.s:
.. yama uvāca .. ..
nimiṣeṇāpi no martyamānayāmi mahītalāt ..
āyuḥśeṣeṇa viprendra pūrṇenātha tyajāmi na.. 12 ..
5.26.d:
.. यम उवाच .. ..
निमिषेणापि नो मर्त्यमानयामि महीतलात् ..
आयुःशेषेण विप्रेन्द्र पूर्णेनाथ त्यजामि न.. 12 ..
5.26.m:
Yama said:
"I do not bring a mortal from the earth even for a moment [before his time], / nor, O best of brahmins, do I abandon [him] when the remainder of his lifespan is complete.

5.26.s:
tata eva hi me nāma dharmarāja iti smṛtam..
samatvātsarvajaṃtūnāṃ pakṣapātavivarjanāt .. 13 ..
5.26.d:
तत एव हि मे नाम धर्मराज इति स्मृतम्..
समत्वात्सर्वजंतूनां पक्षपातविवर्जनात् .. 13 ..
5.26.m: For precisely this reason my name is remembered as Dharmarāja, / because of impartiality toward all creatures and the absence of partiality.

5.26.s:
tasmādgaccha gṛhaṃ vipra yāvadgātraṃ na dahyate ..
baṃdhubhistava śokārtairnādhunā tatra te sthitiḥ .. 14 ..
5.26.d:
तस्माद्गच्छ गृहं विप्र यावद्गात्रं न दह्यते ..
बंधुभिस्तव शोकार्तैर्नाधुना तत्र ते स्थितिः .. 14 ..
5.26.m: Therefore go home, O brahmin, as long as your body is not burned / by your kinsmen stricken with grief; your place is not here now.

5.26.s:
prārthayasva mano'bhīṣṭaṃ varaṃ brāhmaṇasattama ..
na vṛthā darśanaṃ me syātkathaṃcidapi dehinām .. 15 ..
5.26.d:
प्रार्थयस्व मनोऽभीष्टं वरं ब्राह्मणसत्तम ..
न वृथा दर्शनं मे स्यात्कथंचिदपि देहिनाम् .. 15 ..
5.26.m: Request a boon of your heart's desire, O best of brahmins. / The darśana of me should by no means be in vain for embodied beings."

5.26.s:
.. brāhmaṇa uvāca .. ..
avaśyaṃ yadi gaṃtavyaṃ mayā deva gṛhaṃ punaḥ ..
tanmamācakṣva pṛcchāmi varaścaiṣa bhavenmama .. 16 ..
5.26.d:
.. ब्राह्मण उवाच .. ..
अवश्यं यदि गंतव्यं मया देव गृहं पुनः ..
तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छामि वरश्चैष भवेन्मम .. 16 ..
5.26.m:
The brahmin said:
"If I must inevitably go home again, O god, / then explain to me what I ask, and let this be my boon:

5.26.s:
ete ye narakā raudrāḥ sevitāḥ pāpakarmabhiḥ ..
dṛśyaṃte vada kaḥ kena karmaṇā sevyate janaiḥ .. 17 ..
5.26.d:
एते ये नरका रौद्राः सेविताः पापकर्मभिः ..
दृश्यंते वद कः केन कर्मणा सेव्यते जनैः .. 17 ..
5.26.m: These terrible hells that are inhabited by those who perform evil deeds / are seen [here]; tell me, which [hell] is inhabited by people on account of what deed?"

5.26.s:
.. yama uvāca .. ..
asaṃkhyā narakā vipra yathā prāṇigaṇāḥ kṣitau ..
kṛtsnaśaḥ kathituṃ śakyā naivavarṣaśatairapi .. 18 ..
5.26.d:
.. यम उवाच .. ..
असंख्या नरका विप्र यथा प्राणिगणाः क्षितौ ..
कृत्स्नशः कथितुं शक्या नैववर्षशतैरपि .. 18 ..
5.26.m:
Yama said:
"Hells are innumerable, O brahmin, just as the hosts of living beings upon the earth; / they cannot possibly be told in their entirety, even in hundreds of years.

5.26.s:
kīrtayiṣyāmi teṣāṃ te prādhānyena dvijottama ..
ekaviṃśatisaṃkhyā ye pāpilokakṛte kṛtāḥ .. 19 ..
5.26.d:
कीर्तयिष्यामि तेषां ते प्राधान्येन द्विजोत्तम ..
एकविंशतिसंख्या ये पापिलोककृते कृताः .. 19 ..
5.26.m: I shall recount the principal ones among them to you, O best of the twice-born, / which, twenty-one in number, were made for sinful people.

5.26.s:
ādyo'yaṃ rauravo nāma narako dvijasattama ..
prataptatailakuṃbheṣu pacyaṃte yatra jaṃtavaḥ .. 6.26.20 ..
5.26.d:
आद्योऽयं रौरवो नाम नरको द्विजसत्तम ..
प्रतप्ततैलकुंभेषु पच्यंते यत्र जंतवः .. 6.26.20 ..
5.26.m: This first hell, named Raurava, O best of the twice-born, / is where creatures are cooked in cauldrons of heated oil.

5.26.s:
hā mātastāta putreti prakurvaṃti sudāruṇam..
parapākaratāḥ kṣudrāḥ paradravyā pahārakāḥ .. 21 ..
5.26.d:
हा मातस्तात पुत्रेति प्रकुर्वंति सुदारुणम्..
परपाकरताः क्षुद्राः परद्रव्या पहारकाः .. 21 ..
5.26.m: Vile men who take pleasure in others' cooking and who steal the property of others, / utter the most terrible cry: 'Ah mother, father, son!'

5.26.s:
dvitīya eṣa vipreṃdra mahārauravasaṃjñitaḥ ..
kṛtaghnaiḥ sevyate nityaṃ tathā ca gurutalpagaiḥ..22 ..
5.26.d:
द्वितीय एष विप्रेंद्र महारौरवसंज्ञितः ..
कृतघ्नैः सेव्यते नित्यं तथा च गुरुतल्पगैः..22 ..
5.26.m: This second [hell], O best of brahmins, known as Mahāraurava, / is continually inhabited by the ungrateful and by violators of the guru's bed,

5.26.s:
rorūyamāṇairdāhārtaiḥ pacyamānai rhavirbhujā ..
khaṃḍaśaḥ kriyamāṇaiśca tīkṣṇaśastrairanekadhā .. 23 ..
5.26.d:
रोरूयमाणैर्दाहार्तैः पच्यमानै र्हविर्भुजा ..
खंडशः क्रियमाणैश्च तीक्ष्णशस्त्रैरनेकधा .. 23 ..
5.26.m: screaming loudly, afflicted with burning, cooked by fire, / and cut into pieces in many ways with sharp weapons.

5.26.s:
tṛtīyoṃ'dhatamonāma narakaḥ subhayāvahaḥ ..
atra ye puruṣā yāṃti tāṃśca vakṣyāmi sudvija .. 24 ..
5.26.d:
तृतीयोंऽधतमोनाम नरकः सुभयावहः ..
अत्र ये पुरुषा यांति तांश्च वक्ष्यामि सुद्विज .. 24 ..
5.26.m: The third hell is named Andhatamas, which is extremely terrifying. / Which men go there, those too I will tell you, O good twice-born.

5.26.s:
duṣṭena cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭāḥ paradārā narādhamaiḥ ..
sulohāsyāḥ khagāsteṣāṃ haraṃtyatra vilocane .. 29 ..
caturtho'yaṃ prataptākhyo narakaḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ ..
atra te yātanāṃ bhuktvā tathā śuddhā bhavaṃti ca .. 26 ..
yaiḥ kṛtā satataṃ niṃdā gurudevatapasvi nām..
teṣāmutpāṭyate jihvā jātājātā'tra bhūriśaḥ .. 27 ..
eṣo'nyaḥ paṃcamo nāma suprasiddho vidārakaḥ ..
mitradroharatāścātra cchidyaṃte karapatrakaiḥ .. 28 ..
prataptavālukāpūrṇo dhmāyate yaśca vahninā ..
nikumbha iti vikhyātaḥ ṣaṣṭho lokabhayāvahaḥ .. 29 ..
5.26.d:
दुष्टेन चक्षुषा दृष्टाः परदारा नराधमैः ..
सुलोहास्याः खगास्तेषां हरंत्यत्र विलोचने .. 29 ..
चतुर्थोऽयं प्रतप्ताख्यो नरकः संप्रकीर्तितः ..
अत्र ते यातनां भुक्त्वा तथा शुद्धा भवंति च .. 26 ..
यैः कृता सततं निंदा गुरुदेवतपस्वि नाम्..
तेषामुत्पाट्यते जिह्वा जाताजाताऽत्र भूरिशः .. 27 ..
एषोऽन्यः पंचमो नाम सुप्रसिद्धो विदारकः ..
मित्रद्रोहरताश्चात्र च्छिद्यंते करपत्रकैः .. 28 ..
प्रतप्तवालुकापूर्णो ध्मायते यश्च वह्निना ..
निकुम्भ इति विख्यातः षष्ठो लोकभयावहः .. 29 ..
5.26.m:
Vile men by whom another's wife has been looked upon with a wicked eye— / birds with iron beaks tear out their eyes here.
This fourth hell is proclaimed by the name Prataptaka. / Having endured torture here, they thus become purified.
Those by whom constant censure of gurus, gods, and ascetics was made, / of them the tongue is torn out repeatedly as soon as it regrows here.
This other, fifth [hell] is widely renowned by the name Vidāraka; / and here those devoted to betraying friends are cut with saws.
Filled with heated sand, and blazing with fire, / the sixth [hell], celebrated as Nikuṃbha, causes terror to the world.

5.26.s:
prāṇāṃtikaṃ purā dattaṃ yairduḥkhaṃ prāṇināṃ naraiḥ ..
aparādhaṃ vinā te'tra pacyaṃte vālukotkaraiḥ .. 6.26.30 ..
5.26.d:
प्राणांतिकं पुरा दत्तं यैर्दुःखं प्राणिनां नरैः ..
अपराधं विना तेऽत्र पच्यंते वालुकोत्करैः .. 6.26.30 ..
5.26.m: Men by whom mortal distress was formerly inflicted on living beings / without fault are cooked here by piles of sand.

5.26.s:
bībhatsuriti vikhyātaḥ saptamo narakādhamaḥ ..
mūtrāmedhya samākīrṇaḥ samaṃtādatigarhitaḥ .. 31 ..
5.26.d:
बीभत्सुरिति विख्यातः सप्तमो नरकाधमः ..
मूत्रामेध्य समाकीर्णः समंतादतिगर्हितः .. 31 ..
5.26.m: Renowned as Bībhatsa, the seventh is the lowest of hells, / full of urine and excrement, thoroughly vile on every side.

5.26.s:
rājagāmi ca paiśunyaṃ yaiḥ kṛtaṃ sudurātmabhiḥ ..
amedhyapūrṇavaktrāste dhāryaṃte'tra narādhamāḥ .. 32 ..
5.26.d:
राजगामि च पैशुन्यं यैः कृतं सुदुरात्मभिः ..
अमेध्यपूर्णवक्त्रास्ते धार्यंतेऽत्र नराधमाः .. 32 ..
5.26.m: Those most wicked souls by whom slander was brought before a king— / those lowest of men are kept here with mouths filled with excrement.

5.26.s:
kutsitonāma vikhyāto dvijāyaṃ cāṣṭamo'dhamaḥ ..
śleṣmamūtrābhisaṃpūrṇaistathā gandhaiśca kutsitaiḥ .. 33 ..
5.26.d:
कुत्सितोनाम विख्यातो द्विजायं चाष्टमोऽधमः ..
श्लेष्ममूत्राभिसंपूर्णैस्तथा गन्धैश्च कुत्सितैः .. 33 ..
5.26.m: Renowned by the name Kutsita, O twice-born, is this vile eighth [hell], / completely filled with phlegm and urine, and with foul smells.

5.26.s:
gurudevātithibhyaśca svabhṛtyebhyo viśeṣataḥ ..
adattvā bhojanaṃ yaistu kṛtaṃ te'tra vyavasthitāḥ .. 34 ..
5.26.d:
गुरुदेवातिथिभ्यश्च स्वभृत्येभ्यो विशेषतः ..
अदत्त्वा भोजनं यैस्तु कृतं तेऽत्र व्यवस्थिताः .. 34 ..
5.26.m: Those who ate food without having given [it] to their guru, the gods, guests, / and especially to their own servants, are stationed here.

5.26.s:
eṣa durgamanāmā ca navamo dvijasattama ..
tīkṣṇakaṃṭakasaṃkīrṇaḥ sarpavṛścikasaṃkulaḥ .. .. 35 ..
5.26.d:
एष दुर्गमनामा च नवमो द्विजसत्तम ..
तीक्ष्णकंटकसंकीर्णः सर्पवृश्चिकसंकुलः .. .. 35 ..
5.26.m: This ninth [hell], named Durgama, O best of the twice-born, / is beset with sharp thorns and swarming with snakes and scorpions.

5.26.s:
ekasārthaprayātāya kṣutkṣāmāyāvasīdate ..
adattvā bhojanaṃ yaiśca kṛtaṃ te'tra vyavasthitāḥ .. 36 ..
5.26.d:
एकसार्थप्रयाताय क्षुत्क्षामायावसीदते ..
अदत्त्वा भोजनं यैश्च कृतं तेऽत्र व्यवस्थिताः .. 36 ..
5.26.m: Those who ate food without giving [it] to a travel companion / exhausted by hunger and sinking down, are stationed here.

5.26.s:
daśamo'yaṃ suvikhyāto narako nāmaduḥ sahaḥ ..
taptalohamayaiḥ staṃbhaiḥ samaṃtātparivāritaḥ .. 37 ..
5.26.d:
दशमोऽयं सुविख्यातो नरको नामदुः सहः ..
तप्तलोहमयैः स्तंभैः समंतात्परिवारितः .. 37 ..
5.26.m: This well-known tenth hell is named Duḥsaha; / it is surrounded on all sides by pillars made of heated iron.

5.26.s:
ye pāpāḥ paradāreṣu raktā miṣṭāmiṣeṣu vā ..
taptalohamayānstaṃbhāṃste'trāliṃgaṃti mānavāḥ .. .. 38 ..
5.26.d:
ये पापाः परदारेषु रक्ता मिष्टामिषेषु वा ..
तप्तलोहमयान्स्तंभांस्तेऽत्रालिंगंति मानवाः .. .. 38 ..
5.26.m: Those sinful men who were attached to another's wife or to sweet meats, / embrace pillars made of heated iron here.

5.26.s:
ekādaśo'paraścāyamākarṣākhyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ..
narako vipraśārdūla taptasaṃdaṃśasaṃkulaḥ .. 39 ..
5.26.d:
एकादशोऽपरश्चायमाकर्षाख्यः प्रकीर्तितः ..
नरको विप्रशार्दूल तप्तसंदंशसंकुलः .. 39 ..
5.26.m: This other, eleventh hell is proclaimed by the name Ākarṣa, / O tiger among brahmins, filled with heated pincers.

5.26.s:
strīvipragurudevānāṃ vittaṃ cāśnaṃti ye narāḥ ..
saṃdaṃśairapi kṛṣyaṃte tatra taptaiḥ samaṃtataḥ .. 6.26.40 ..
5.26.d:
स्त्रीविप्रगुरुदेवानां वित्तं चाश्नंति ये नराः ..
संदंशैरपि कृष्यंते तत्र तप्तैः समंततः .. 6.26.40 ..
5.26.m: Those men who consume the wealth of women, brahmins, gurus, and the gods, / are dragged around on every side there by heated pincers.

5.26.s:
saṃdaṃśo dvādaśaścāyaṃ tathā'bhakṣyaprabhakṣakāḥ ..
lohadaṃtamukhairgṛdhairbhakṣyaṃte'tra narādhamāḥ .. 41 ..
5.26.d:
संदंशो द्वादशश्चायं तथाऽभक्ष्यप्रभक्षकाः ..
लोहदंतमुखैर्गृधैर्भक्ष्यंतेऽत्र नराधमाः .. 41 ..
5.26.m: The twelfth is Saṃdaṃśa; those who devour inedible things, / those lowest of men, are devoured here by vultures with iron-toothed mouths.

5.26.s:
eṣa trayodaśonāma suvikhyāto niyaṃtrakaḥ ..
samaṃtātkṛmibhirvyāptastathā ca dṛḍhabandhanaiḥ .. 42 ..
5.26.d:
एष त्रयोदशोनाम सुविख्यातो नियंत्रकः ..
समंतात्कृमिभिर्व्याप्तस्तथा च दृढबन्धनैः .. 42 ..
5.26.m: This thirteenth [hell] is widely renowned by the name Niyantraka, / infested with worms on all sides and having tight fetters.

5.26.s:
nyāsāpahārakāḥ pāpāstatra baddhāśca baṃdhanaiḥ ..
kṛmivṛścika kīṭādyairbhakṣyate dvijasattama .. 43 ..
5.26.d:
न्यासापहारकाः पापास्तत्र बद्धाश्च बंधनैः ..
कृमिवृश्चिक कीटाद्यैर्भक्ष्यते द्विजसत्तम .. 43 ..
5.26.m: Sinners who steal deposits, bound there with fetters, / are eaten by worms, scorpions, insects, and the like, O best of the twice-born.

5.26.s:
tathā caturdaśonāma narako'dhomukhaḥ sthitaḥ ..
narakāṇāṃ samastānāmeṣa raudratamākṛtiḥ .. 44 ..
5.26.d:
तथा चतुर्दशोनाम नरकोऽधोमुखः स्थितः ..
नरकाणां समस्तानामेष रौद्रतमाकृतिः .. 44 ..
5.26.m: Likewise, the fourteenth hell is established by the name Adhomukha; / of all the hells, this one has the most terrible form.

5.26.s:
atra cādhomukhā baddhā vṛkṣaśākhāvalaṃbitāḥ ..
pacyaṃte vahninā'dhastādbrahmaghnā ye ca mānavāḥ .. 45 ..
5.26.d:
अत्र चाधोमुखा बद्धा वृक्षशाखावलंबिताः ..
पच्यंते वह्निनाऽधस्ताद्ब्रह्मघ्ना ये च मानवाः .. 45 ..
5.26.m: And bound head-downwards here, suspended from branches of trees, / those men who are slayers of brahmins are cooked by fire from below.

5.26.s:
yūkāmatkuṇadaṃśādyaiḥ saṃkīrṇo'yaṃ dvijottama ..
narako bhīṣaṇo nāma khyātaḥ pañcadaśo mahān .. 46 ..
5.26.d:
यूकामत्कुणदंशाद्यैः संकीर्णोऽयं द्विजोत्तम ..
नरको भीषणो नाम ख्यातः पञ्चदशो महान् .. 46 ..
5.26.m: Teeming with lice, bugs, biting insects, and the like, O best of the twice-born, / the great fifteenth hell is renowned by the name Bhīṣaṇa.

5.26.s:
kūṭasākṣyaratānāṃ ca tathaivānṛtavādinām ..
atrāśrayo mayā dattastathānyeṣāṃ kukarmiṇām .. 47 ..
5.26.d:
कूटसाक्ष्यरतानां च तथैवानृतवादिनाम् ..
अत्राश्रयो मया दत्तस्तथान्येषां कुकर्मिणाम् .. 47 ..
5.26.m: For those intent on false testimony and likewise for liars, / a dwelling has been provided here by me, as well as for other evildoers.

5.26.s:
eṣa ṣoḍaśa uddiṣṭo narako nāma kṣudradaḥ ..
yudhārtairmānavairvyāptaḥ samaṃtāddvijasattama ..49..
mṛṣṭamāṃsāni yaiḥ pāpairbhakṣitāni dvijanmabhiḥ ..
kṣudhārtāste nijaṃ kāyaṃ bhakṣayaṃtyatra saṃsthitāḥ .. 49 ..
5.26.d:
एष षोडश उद्दिष्टो नरको नाम क्षुद्रदः ..
युधार्तैर्मानवैर्व्याप्तः समंताद्द्विजसत्तम ..49..
मृष्टमांसानि यैः पापैर्भक्षितानि द्विजन्मभिः ..
क्षुधार्तास्ते निजं कायं भक्षयंत्यत्र संस्थिताः .. 49 ..
5.26.m:
This sixteenth hell indicated is named Kṣudrada; / it is filled on all sides with men tormented by hunger, O best of the twice-born.
Those sinners who, though twice-born, have eaten seasoned meat, / being afflicted with hunger, stay here eating their own bodies. 49

5.26.s:
tathā saptadaśaścāyaṃ kṣārākhyo narakaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
sukṣāreṇa samākīrṇaḥ sarvaprāṇibhayāvahaḥ .. 6.26.50 ..
5.26.d:
तथा सप्तदशश्चायं क्षाराख्यो नरकः स्मृतः ..
सुक्षारेण समाकीर्णः सर्वप्राणिभयावहः .. 6.26.50 ..
5.26.m: And so this seventeenth hell is known by the name of Kṣāra; / it is filled with strong alkaline caustic and brings fear to all living beings. 50

5.26.s:
vratabhaṃgakarā ye ca ye ca pāṣaṇḍino narāḥ ..
te'trāgatya śitaiḥ śastraiḥ piṣyaṃte pāpakṛttamāḥ .. 51 ..
5.26.d:
व्रतभंगकरा ये च ये च पाषण्डिनो नराः ..
तेऽत्रागत्य शितैः शस्त्रैः पिष्यंते पापकृत्तमाः .. 51 ..
5.26.m: And those men who break their vows, and those who are heretics— / coming here, those worst of evildoers are ground up by sharp weapons. 51

5.26.s:
eṣa cāṣṭādaśo nāma kathitaśca nidāghakaḥ ..
jvalitāṃgārasaṃkīrṇo duḥsevyaḥ sarvadehinām .. 52 ..
5.26.d:
एष चाष्टादशो नाम कथितश्च निदाघकः ..
ज्वलितांगारसंकीर्णो दुःसेव्यः सर्वदेहिनाम् .. 52 ..
5.26.m: And this eighteenth is declared by the name Nidāghaka; / filled with blazing coals, it is painful to endure for all embodied beings. 52

5.26.s:
dūṣayaṃti ca ye śāstraṃ kāvyaṃ vipraṃ ca kanyakām ..
aṃgārāṃtaḥ sthitāte'tra dhriyaṃte mānavā dvija .. .. 53 ..
5.26.d:
दूषयंति च ये शास्त्रं काव्यं विप्रं च कन्यकाम् ..
अंगारांतः स्थितातेऽत्र ध्रियंते मानवा द्विज .. .. 53 ..
5.26.m: Those who defame scripture, poetry, a brahmin, and an unmarried maiden— / those men are held here staying amidst the coals, O twice-born. 53

5.26.s:
ekonaviṃśatiścāyaṃ prakhyātaḥ kūṭaśālmaliḥ ..
sutīkṣṇakaṃṭakākīrṇaḥ samaṃtāddvijasattama .ā 54 ..
5.26.d:
एकोनविंशतिश्चायं प्रख्यातः कूटशाल्मलिः ..
सुतीक्ष्णकंटकाकीर्णः समंताद्द्विजसत्तम .आ 54 ..
5.26.m: And this nineteenth is renowned as Kūṭaśālmali; / it is covered all around with extremely sharp thorns, O best of the twice-born. 54

5.26.s:
nāstikā bhinnamaryādā ye ca viprasya ghātakāḥ ..
te sarve'tra narā nityamāruhaṃti pataṃti ca ..95..
eṣa viṃśatimo nāma narako dvijasattama ..
asipatravanākhyaśca kaṣṭasevyo durātmabhiḥ .. .. 56 ..
atra yāṃti narā vipra pararaṃdhranirīkṣakāḥ ..
kūṭakarmaratā ye ca śāstravikrayakārakāḥ .. 57 ..
ekaviṃśatimā caiṣā nāmnā vaitaraṇī nadī ..
sarvaireva narairgamyā dharmapāpānuyāyibhiḥ .. 58 ..
mṛtyukāle samutpanne dhenuṃ yacchaṃti ye narāḥ ..
tasyā lāṃgūlamāśritya tārayaṃti sukhena ca .. 59 ..
adattvā gāṃ ca ye martyā mriyaṃte dvijasattama ..
tīrtvā hastādibhirdurgā ta imāṃ saṃtaraṃti ca .. 6.26.60...
etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'smi dvijottama ..
vistareṇa tava prītyā svarūpaṃ narakodbhavam..61...
5.26.d:
नास्तिका भिन्नमर्यादा ये च विप्रस्य घातकाः ..
ते सर्वेऽत्र नरा नित्यमारुहंति पतंति च ..95..
एष विंशतिमो नाम नरको द्विजसत्तम ..
असिपत्रवनाख्यश्च कष्टसेव्यो दुरात्मभिः .. .. 56 ..
अत्र यांति नरा विप्र पररंध्रनिरीक्षकाः ..
कूटकर्मरता ये च शास्त्रविक्रयकारकाः .. 57 ..
एकविंशतिमा चैषा नाम्ना वैतरणी नदी ..
सर्वैरेव नरैर्गम्या धर्मपापानुयायिभिः .. 58 ..
मृत्युकाले समुत्पन्ने धेनुं यच्छंति ये नराः ..
तस्या लांगूलमाश्रित्य तारयंति सुखेन च .. 59 ..
अदत्त्वा गां च ये मर्त्या म्रियंते द्विजसत्तम ..
तीर्त्वा हस्तादिभिर्दुर्गा त इमां संतरंति च .. 6.26.60...
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यत्पृष्टोऽस्मि द्विजोत्तम ..
विस्तरेण तव प्रीत्या स्वरूपं नरकोद्भवम्..61...
5.26.m:
Atheists, transgressors of proper boundaries, and those who murder a brahmin— / all those men perpetually climb up and fall down here. 55
This twentieth hell, O best of the twice-born, / is named Asipatravana, and it is painfully endured by the wicked. 56
To this place go men, O brahmin, who spy on the faults of others, / those devoted to deceitful deeds, and those who sell sacred scriptures. 57
And this twenty-first is the river called Vaitaraṇī, / which must be crossed by all men, followers of righteousness or sin. 58
Those men who, when the time of death arrives, give a cow, / cross over with ease by clinging to its tail. 59
And mortals who die without giving a cow, O best of the twice-born, / cross over this difficult [stream] swimming with their hands and other limbs. 60
All this, concerning which I was asked, has been related to you, O best of the twice-born, / in detail, out of affection for you—the nature of hell. 61

5.26.s:
tasmādgaccha gṛhaṃ śīghraṃ yāvadgātraṃ na dahyate..
bandhubhistava śokārtairgṛhītvā vāṃchitaṃ dhanam .. 62 .. ..

5.26.m:
Therefore, go home quickly before your body is burned / by your relatives, who are stricken with grief, having taken their desired wealth. 62
The brahmin said: / If, O lord, I must indeed go to my own home, / then tell me by what deed a man does not go to hell. 63
Yama said: / One who is devoted to pilgrimage to sacred fords, always worships deities and guests, / is friendly to brahmins and offers refuge—such a man does not go to hell. 64
One engaged in benevolence toward others, always devoted to silent prayer, / and constantly absorbed in scriptural study—such a one does not go to hell, O twice-born. 65
The man who continually constructs stepped wells, wells, ponds, / and shrines to the deities does not see hell. 66
He who gives fire in the cold season, provides water in the summer, / and provides shelter in the rains does not see hell. 67
One endowed with vows and fasting, of tranquil soul, with senses subdued, / celibate, and always meditative—such a man does not go to hell. 68

तीर्थं वा जपहोमं वा सर्वलोकसुखावहम् .. 73 ..

5.26.m:
The man who is a giver of food, especially a giver of sesame seeds, / and devoted to non-violence does not see hell. 69
One accomplished in Vedic study, dedicated to scripture, of pleasant speech, / and always devoted to righteous discourse does not see hell. 70
The brahmin said: / Even a fool knows this: a man who performs good deeds / does not go to hell, whereas one devoted to sinful actions [does]. 71
Therefore, tell me by what deed even one who has done evil deeds / quickly destroys sin, even by a small [act], and a man then goes to heaven. 72
Tell me that, O best of gods, whether a vow or a observance, / a sacred ford, or recitation and oblation, which brings happiness to all people. 73
Yama said: / Here I shall tell you a very great secret, O best of the twice-born; / it should always be carefully guarded according to my word. 74
By performing which deed even a person endowed with great sins / does not go to the hell that causes torment. 75

5.26.m:
In the region of Ānarta there is a delightful, auspicious sacred field, embodying all sacred fords, / born of Hāṭakeśvara, which destroys great sins. 76
Whoever worships Hara there with devotion even for half a month, / though burdened with all sins, is honored in the world of Śiva. 77
Therefore, having gone there swiftly, worship Śaṃkara, / whereby you will attain final liberation along with ten generations. 78
Sūta said: / Having heard the instruction of the king of righteousness, when he, delighted, / set out toward his home, the sweet city [of Mathurā], 79
just then a messenger arrived, bringing the second Gokarṇa, / and having seized him, quickly presented him before the king of righteousness. 80
Then the king of righteousness, overjoyed, spoke to that messenger, / having seen Gokarṇa before him and the other departing for home: 81
“Since this brahmin was brought by you after the proper time had elapsed, / therefore release him also quickly along with the second one.” 82

5.26.d:
ततस्तौ तत्क्षणान्मुक्तौ गोकर्णौ ब्राह्मणौ समम् ..
स्वंस्वं कलेवरं प्राप्य सहसाथ समन्वितौ .. 83 ..

यमोपदेशसंजुष्टो द्वितीयाय सविस्तरम् .. 84 ..

देवतायतनैर्व्याप्तं क्षेत्रं दृष्ट्वाऽखिलं ततः .. 85 ..

हाटकेश्वरजं क्षेत्रं संप्राप्य तपसि द्रुतम् .. 86 ..

सशरीरौ दिवं प्राप्तौ तत्प्रभावाद्विजोत्तमाः .. 87 ..

5.26.m:
Then, released immediately at that moment, the two brahmins named Gokarṇa together / reached their respective bodies and were at once reanimated. 83
Then that first twice-born Gokarṇa, endowed with the instruction of Yama, / recounted everything in detail to the second one. 84
Then, having abandoned their homes, both Gokarṇas remained [there], / having then seen the entire sacred field filled with shrines to the deities. 85
Two liṅgas were established by the two on the southern and northern boundaries, / and having reached the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara, they swiftly engaged in austerity. 86
Then, having properly worshipped Śiva and performed austerity as prescribed, / they attained heaven in bodily form by that power, O best of the twice-born. 87
A night-vigil was performed by both on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa; / whatever man performs it with devotion goes to Śiva’s abode. 88
A childless man obtains sons, one desiring wealth will attain wealth, / and a desireless person surely attains liberation; there is no doubt. 89

5.26.m:
Sūta said: / All this has been related to you, O best of the twice-born—the boundary / and the extent of this sacred field in the four directions in detail. 90
And whatever men dwell within it, O best of brahmins, / even those engaged in agriculture attain the supreme state; / how much more so those of restrained mind, peaceful, self-controlled, and with subdued senses! 91
Even insects, winged creatures, beasts, birds, and game, / dying in that sacred field, go to the heavenly world, without doubt. 92
How much more so those men who, after resolving to fast unto death there, / have renounced the world, endowed with faith, with Janārdana residing in their hearts! 93
Therefore, with every effort, that sacred field is indeed to be served, / especially when the Kali age has arrived, engulfed in sin. 94
All sacred fords purify by means of ritual ablution and gifts, without doubt; / but the sacred field originating from Hāṭakeśvara purifies through merely residing [there]. 95

5.26.m: Wherever there is water—in step-wells, wells, and tanks, O brahmins— / having bathed there, a man is freed from all sins. 96

5.26.m: What use are sacrifices? What use are vain gifts? What use are vows, or even recitations? / Dwelling made in that sacred field is better for those who desire heaven. 97

5.26.m:
This is purifying, granting longevity, auspicious, and destroying sin / for those who constantly listen to the māhātmya of the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara. 98
Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of Gokarnatīrtha,' in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Sacred Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. 26.

5.27.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
imamarthaṃ purā pṛṣṭo vāsavena bṛhaspatiḥ ..
yathā provāca vipreṃdrāstadvo vakṣyāmi sāṃpratam .. 2 ..
5.27.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
इममर्थं पुरा पृष्टो वासवेन बृहस्पतिः ..
यथा प्रोवाच विप्रेंद्रास्तद्वो वक्ष्यामि सांप्रतम् .. 2 ..
5.27.m: Sūta said: / When Bṛhaspati was asked about this matter long ago by Vāsava, / as he explained it, O lords of brahmins, that I shall now declare to you. 2

5.27.s:
purā śakraṃ samāsīnaṃ sabhāyāṃ tridaśaiḥ saha ..
saha śacyā mahātmānamupāsāṃcakrire surāḥ .. 3 ..
5.27.d:
पुरा शक्रं समासीनं सभायां त्रिदशैः सह ..
सह शच्या महात्मानमुपासांचक्रिरे सुराः .. 3 ..
5.27.m: Long ago, the gods waited upon the great-souled Śakra, / who was seated in the assembly together with the thirty [gods] and Śacī: 3

5.27.s:
gandharvāpsarasaścaiva siddhavidyādharāśca ye ..
guhyakāḥ kiṃnarā daityā rākṣasā uragāstathā .. 4 ..
5.27.d:
गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव सिद्धविद्याधराश्च ये ..
गुह्यकाः किंनरा दैत्या राक्षसा उरगास्तथा .. 4 ..
5.27.m: Gandharvas and apsarases, siddhas and vidyādharas, / guhyakas, kiṃnaras, daityas, rākṣasas, and uragas; 4

5.27.s:
kalāḥ kāṣṭhānimeṣāśca nakṣatrāṇi grahāstathā ..
sāṃgā vedāstathā mūrtāstīrthānyāyatanāni ca .. 5 ...
5.27.d:
कलाः काष्ठानिमेषाश्च नक्षत्राणि ग्रहास्तथा ..
सांगा वेदास्तथा मूर्तास्तीर्थान्यायतनानि च .. 5 ...
5.27.m: kalās, kāṣṭhās, nimeṣas, constellations, planets, / the Vedas with their auxiliary limbs in embodied form, sacred fords, and shrines. 5

5.27.s:
tathā cakruḥ kathāścitrā devadānavarakṣasām ..
rājarṣīṇāṃ purāṇānāṃ brahmarṣīṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ .. 6 ..
5.27.d:
तथा चक्रुः कथाश्चित्रा देवदानवरक्षसाम् ..
राजर्षीणां पुराणानां ब्रह्मर्षीणां विशेषतः .. 6 ..
5.27.m: So too they narrated varied tales of gods, dānavas, and rakṣases, / of ancient royal seers, and especially of brahmin seers. 6

5.27.s:
kasmiṃścidatha saṃprāpte prastāve tridaśeśvaraḥ ..
papraccha vinayopeto vipraśreṣṭhaṃ bṛhaspatim .. 7 ..
5.27.d:
कस्मिंश्चिदथ संप्राप्ते प्रस्तावे त्रिदशेश्वरः ..
पप्रच्छ विनयोपेतो विप्रश्रेष्ठं बृहस्पतिम् .. 7 ..
5.27.m: Then, on a certain occasion that arose, the lord of the thirty [gods], / endowed with humility, questioned Bṛhaspati, the best of brahmins: 7

5.27.s:
bhagavañchrotumicchāmi pramāṇaṃ yugasaṃbhavam ..
māhātmyaṃ ca svarūpaṃ ca yathāvadvaktumarhasi .. 8 ..
5.27.d:
भगवञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि प्रमाणं युगसंभवम् ..
माहात्म्यं च स्वरूपं च यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि .. 8 ..
5.27.m: "O Blessed One, I desire to hear the duration belonging to the yugas, / their māhātmya, and their true nature. You should declare it properly." 8

5.27.s:
.. bṛhaspati ruvāca .. ..
ahaṃ te kīrtayiṣyāmi māhātmyaṃ yugasaṃbhavam ..
yatpramāṇaṃ svarūpaṃ ca śṛṇuṣvāvahitaḥ sthitaḥ .. 9 ..
5.27.d:
.. बृहस्पति रुवाच .. ..
अहं ते कीर्तयिष्यामि माहात्म्यं युगसंभवम् ..
यत्प्रमाणं स्वरूपं च शृणुष्वावहितः स्थितः .. 9 ..
5.27.m: Bṛhaspati said: / I shall proclaim to you the māhātmya belonging to the yugas, / their duration, and their nature. Listen with an attentive mind. 9

5.27.s:
aṣṭāviṃśatisahasrāṇi lakṣāḥ saptadaśaiva tu ..
pramāṇena kṛtaṃ proktaṃ yatra śuklo janārdanaḥ..6.27.10....
5.27.d:
अष्टाविंशतिसहस्राणि लक्षाः सप्तदशैव तु ..
प्रमाणेन कृतं प्रोक्तं यत्र शुक्लो जनार्दनः..6.27.10....
5.27.m: Seventeen hundred thousand and twenty-eight thousand [years] / is declared to be the extent of the Kṛta [yuga], wherein Janārdana is white. 10

5.27.s:
catuṣpādastathā dharmaḥ susaṃpūrṇā vasundharā ..
kāmakrodhavinirmuktā bhayadveṣavivarjitāḥ......
janāścirāyuṣastatra śāntātmāno jitendriyāḥ ..
pañcatālapramāṇāśca dīptimanto bahuśrutāḥ .. 12 ..
5.27.d:
चतुष्पादस्तथा धर्मः सुसंपूर्णा वसुन्धरा ..
कामक्रोधविनिर्मुक्ता भयद्वेषविवर्जिताः......
जनाश्चिरायुषस्तत्र शान्तात्मानो जितेन्द्रियाः ..
पञ्चतालप्रमाणाश्च दीप्तिमन्तो बहुश्रुताः .. 12 ..
5.27.m: Dharma is four-footed, and the earth is exceedingly bountiful; / freed from desire and anger, devoid of fear and hatred, / people there are long-lived, peaceful in mind, with senses subdued, / five tālas in height, radiant, and deeply learned. 12

5.27.s:
tatra ṣoḍaśasāhasraṃ bālatvaṃ jāyate nṛṇām ..
tataśca yauvanaṃ proktaṃ dvātriṃśadyāvadeva hi .. 13 ..
5.27.d:
तत्र षोडशसाहस्रं बालत्वं जायते नृणाम् ..
ततश्च यौवनं प्रोक्तं द्वात्रिंशद्यावदेव हि .. 13 ..
5.27.m: There, childhood of men lasts for sixteen thousand [years]; / after that, youth is declared to last up to thirty-two [thousand]. 13

5.27.s:
tataḥ paraṃ ca vārddhakyaṃ śanaiḥ saṃjāyate nṛṇām..
lakṣāṃte paramaṃ yāvadanyeṣāmadhikaṃ kvacit .. 14 ..
tatra sattvāśca ye kecitpaśavaḥ pakṣiṇo mṛgāḥ ..
daivīṃ vācaṃ prajalpaṃti na virodhaṃ vrajaṃti ca .ā15..
krīḍaṃti nakulaiḥ sarpā biḍālā mūṣakaiḥ samam ..
pañcānanairmṛgā nityamulūkāścāpi vāyasaiḥ ...6..
akṛṣṭā ca mahī sasyaṃ janayatyati bhūriśaḥ ..
vrīhimudgayavaprāyaṃ susvādu balavṛddhidam ...7..
sarvartuphalino vṛkṣāḥ sapuṣpaphaladhāriṇaḥ ..
supatrāḥ kaṃṭakairhīnāḥ kalpapādapasaṃnibhāḥ...8..
5.27.d:
ततः परं च वार्द्धक्यं शनैः संजायते नृणाम्..
लक्षांते परमं यावदन्येषामधिकं क्वचित् .. 14 ..
तत्र सत्त्वाश्च ये केचित्पशवः पक्षिणो मृगाः ..
दैवीं वाचं प्रजल्पंति न विरोधं व्रजंति च .आ15..
क्रीडंति नकुलैः सर्पा बिडाला मूषकैः समम् ..
पञ्चाननैर्मृगा नित्यमुलूकाश्चापि वायसैः ...6..
अकृष्टा च मही सस्यं जनयत्यति भूरिशः ..
व्रीहिमुद्गयवप्रायं सुस्वादु बलवृद्धिदम् ...7..
सर्वर्तुफलिनो वृक्षाः सपुष्पफलधारिणः ..
सुपत्राः कंटकैर्हीनाः कल्पपादपसंनिभाः...8..
5.27.m:
Thereafter, old age gradually comes upon men, / lasting up to a maximum of one hundred thousand, and for some, somewhere, even more. 14
And whatever beings are there—beasts, birds, and game— / speak divine speech and enter into no enmity. 15 / Serpents play with mongooses, cats together with mice, / deer constantly with lions, and owls even with crows. 16
And the unplowed earth yields abundant crops, / mostly rice, mung beans, and barley, exceedingly sweet and increasing strength. 17
Trees bear fruit in all seasons, laden with flowers and fruits, / with beautiful leaves, free of thorns, resembling the wish-fulfilling tree. 18

5.27.s:
dhenavaśca prayacchaṃti vāṃchitaṃ svādu satpayaḥ ..
sarveṣvapi hi kāleṣu bhūri sarppiḥpradaṃ nṛṇām.. 19 ..
5.27.d:
धेनवश्च प्रयच्छंति वांछितं स्वादु सत्पयः ..
सर्वेष्वपि हि कालेषु भूरि सर्प्पिःप्रदं नृणाम्.. 19 ..
5.27.m: And cows yield desired, sweet, excellent milk; / in all seasons they grant abundant clarified butter to men. 19

5.27.s:
na tatra vidhavā nārī jāyate na ca durbhagā ..
kākavaṃdhyā sutairhīnā na ca śīlavivarjitā ..6.27.20...
5.27.d:
न तत्र विधवा नारी जायते न च दुर्भगा ..
काकवंध्या सुतैर्हीना न च शीलविवर्जिता ..6.27.20...
5.27.m: There, no woman becomes a widow, nor unfortunate, / nor barren after one child, nor bereft of sons, nor lacking good conduct. 20

5.27.s:
yathājanma tathā mṛtyuḥ kramātsaṃjāyate nṛṇām ..
na vīkṣate pitā putraṃ mṛtaṃ kvāpi kadācana .. 21 ..
5.27.d:
यथाजन्म तथा मृत्युः क्रमात्संजायते नृणाम् ..
न वीक्षते पिता पुत्रं मृतं क्वापि कदाचन .. 21 ..
5.27.m: Just as birth occurs, so death occurs for men in orderly succession; / never does a father behold a son dead anywhere. 21

5.27.s:
na pretatvaṃ ca lokānāṃ mṛtānāṃ tatra jāyate ..
na cāpi narake vāso na ca rogavyathā kvacit .. 22 ..
5.27.d:
न प्रेतत्वं च लोकानां मृतानां तत्र जायते ..
न चापि नरके वासो न च रोगव्यथा क्वचित् .. 22 ..
5.27.m: And the state of a ghost does not befall men who have died there; / nor is there dwelling in hell, nor the affliction of disease anywhere. 22

5.27.s:
vedāṃtagā dvijāḥ sarve nityaṃ svādhyāyaśīlinaḥ ..
vedavyākhyānasaṃhṛṣṭā brahmajñānavicakṣaṇāḥ .. 23 ..
5.27.d:
वेदांतगा द्विजाः सर्वे नित्यं स्वाध्यायशीलिनः ..
वेदव्याख्यानसंहृष्टा ब्रह्मज्ञानविचक्षणाः .. 23 ..
5.27.m: All brahmins are masters of the Vedānta, constantly devoted to self-study, / rejoicing in the exposition of the Vedas, skilled in knowledge of the Absolute. 23

5.27.s:
kṣatriyāścāpi bhūpālamekaṃ kṛtvā subhaktitaḥ ..
tadādeśātprabhuṃjaṃti mahīṃ dharmeṇa nityaśaḥ ..24..
5.27.d:
क्षत्रियाश्चापि भूपालमेकं कृत्वा सुभक्तितः ..
तदादेशात्प्रभुंजंति महीं धर्मेण नित्यशः ..24..
5.27.m: And the kṣatriyas, having made one king with great devotion, / by his command enjoy the earth constantly according to dharma. 24

5.27.s:
vaiśyā vaiśyajanārhāṇi cakruḥ karmāṇi bhūriśaḥ ..
paśupālanapūrvāṇi krayavikrayajāni ca .. 25 ..
5.27.d:
वैश्या वैश्यजनार्हाणि चक्रुः कर्माणि भूरिशः ..
पशुपालनपूर्वाणि क्रयविक्रयजानि च .. 25 ..
5.27.m: Vaiśyas perform in abundance the occupations suitable for vaiśyas, / consisting of cattle-rearing and born of buying and selling. 25

5.27.s:
muktvaikāṃ dvijaśuśrūṣā na śūdrāstatra cakrire ..
kiṃcitkarma suraśreṣṭha śraddhayā parayā yutāḥ .. 26 ..
5.27.d:
मुक्त्वैकां द्विजशुश्रूषा न शूद्रास्तत्र चक्रिरे ..
किंचित्कर्म सुरश्रेष्ठ श्रद्धया परया युताः .. 26 ..
5.27.m: Leaving aside the singular service to the twice-born, the śūdras there do not perform / any other work, O best of the gods, endowed with supreme faith. 26

5.27.s:
na tatra cāṃtyajo jajñe na ca saṃkarasaṃbhavaḥ ..
nāpavitro na varṇānāṃ pañcamo dṛśyate bhuvi .. 27 ..
5.27.d:
न तत्र चांत्यजो जज्ञे न च संकरसंभवः ..
नापवित्रो न वर्णानां पञ्चमो दृश्यते भुवि .. 27 ..
5.27.m: No outcaste is born there, nor does the occurrence of mixed caste arise; / no one is impure, nor is a fifth of the castes seen upon earth. 27

5.27.s:
yajanaṃ yājanaṃ dānaṃ vrataṃ niyama eva ca ..
tīrthayātrāṃ narāstatra niṣkāmā eva kurvate .. 28 ..
5.27.d:
यजनं याजनं दानं व्रतं नियम एव च ..
तीर्थयात्रां नरास्तत्र निष्कामा एव कुर्वते .. 28 ..
5.27.m: Sacrificing, officiating at sacrifices, giving, vows, and observances, / and pilgrimage to sacred fords—men perform these there solely without desire. 28

5.27.s:
evaṃvidhaṃ sahasrākṣa mayā te parikīrtitam ..
ādyaṃ kṛtayugaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvalokasukhāvaham .. 29 ..
5.27.d:
एवंविधं सहस्राक्ष मया ते परिकीर्तितम् ..
आद्यं कृतयुगं पुण्यं सर्वलोकसुखावहम् .. 29 ..
5.27.m: Such as this, O thousand-eyed one, has been proclaimed to you by me— / the initial holy Kṛtayuga, bringing happiness to all the world. 29

5.27.s:
tatastretāyugaṃ nāma dvitīyaṃ saṃpravartate ..
varṣāṇāṃ ṣaṇṇavatyāḍhyā lakṣā dvādaśa saṃkhyayā .. 6.27.30 ..
5.27.d:
ततस्त्रेतायुगं नाम द्वितीयं संप्रवर्तते ..
वर्षाणां षण्णवत्याढ्या लक्षा द्वादश संख्यया .. 6.27.30 ..
5.27.m: Then the second, named Tretāyuga, commences; / in number of years it is twelve hundred thousand endowed with ninety-six [thousand]. 30

5.27.s:
so'pi sākṣājagannāthaḥ śvetadvīpāśrayāśritaḥ ..
tatra raktatvamāyāti bhaga vāngaruḍadhvajaḥ .. 31 ..
5.27.d:
सोऽपि साक्षाजगन्नाथः श्वेतद्वीपाश्रयाश्रितः ..
तत्र रक्तत्वमायाति भग वान्गरुडध्वजः .. 31 ..
5.27.m: Even the lord of the universe himself, who abides in Śvetadvīpa— / the Blessed One whose emblem is Garuḍa—becomes red in color there. 31

5.27.s:
tripādastatra dharmaḥ syātpādenaikena pātakam ..
tenāpi jāyate sparddhā varṇānāmitaretaram .. 32 ..
5.27.d:
त्रिपादस्तत्र धर्मः स्यात्पादेनैकेन पातकम् ..
तेनापि जायते स्पर्द्धा वर्णानामितरेतरम् .. 32 ..
5.27.m: There dharma has three feet, while evil has one foot; / through that alone rivalry arises mutually among the castes. 32

5.27.s:
tataḥ phalāni vāṃchaṃti tīrthayātrodbhavāni te ..
vratānāṃ niyamānāṃ ca svargavāsādihetavaḥ .. 33 ..
5.27.d:
ततः फलानि वांछंति तीर्थयात्रोद्भवानि ते ..
व्रतानां नियमानां च स्वर्गवासादिहेतवः .. 33 ..
5.27.m: Then they desire fruits arising from pilgrimage to sacred fords, / from vows and observances, which are the causes of dwelling in heaven and the like. 33

5.27.s:
tataḥ kāmavaśānmohaṃ sarve gacchaṃti mānavāḥ ..
mohāddrohaṃ tato gatvā pāpaṃ kurvaṃtyanukramāt .. 34 ..
5.27.d:
ततः कामवशान्मोहं सर्वे गच्छंति मानवाः ..
मोहाद्द्रोहं ततो गत्वा पापं कुर्वंत्यनुक्रमात् .. 34 ..
5.27.m: Then, under the sway of desire, all human beings fall into delusion; / having fallen into delusion, they proceed to malice and consecutively commit sin.

5.27.s:
tatastu rauravādīni narakāṇi yamaḥ svayam ..
sajjīkaroti devendra hyekaviṃśatisaṃkhyayā .. 35 ..
5.27.d:
ततस्तु रौरवादीनि नरकाणि यमः स्वयम् ..
सज्जीकरोति देवेन्द्र ह्येकविंशतिसंख्यया .. 35 ..
5.27.m: Thereupon, Yama himself prepares the hells, such as Raurava and others, / twenty-one in number, O lord of the gods.

5.27.s:
karmānusāratastāni sevayaṃti narādhamāḥ ..
kecidanye mahendrādilokānmokṣaṃ tathā pare .. 36 ..
5.27.d:
कर्मानुसारतस्तानि सेवयंति नराधमाः ..
केचिदन्ये महेन्द्रादिलोकान्मोक्षं तथा परे .. 36 ..
5.27.m: According to their actions, base men enter them; / certain others go to the worlds of Mahendra and the rest, and others to liberation.

5.27.s:
trividhāḥ puruṣāstatra śreṣṭhāścādhamamadhyamāḥ ..
trividhāni ca karmāṇi prakurvaṃti sureśvara .. 37 ..
5.27.d:
त्रिविधाः पुरुषास्तत्र श्रेष्ठाश्चाधममध्यमाः ..
त्रिविधानि च कर्माणि प्रकुर्वंति सुरेश्वर .. 37 ..
5.27.m: Threefold are the men there: superior, base, and middling; / and they perform threefold deeds, O lord of gods.

5.27.s:
unnatāstālamātreṇa tejovīryasamanvitāḥ ..
cakruśca kṛṣikarmāṇi vaiśyāścaivānnalipsayā .. 38 ..
5.27.d:
उन्नतास्तालमात्रेण तेजोवीर्यसमन्विताः ..
चक्रुश्च कृषिकर्माणि वैश्याश्चैवान्नलिप्सया .. 38 ..
5.27.m: Tall as a palm tree, endowed with fiery energy and vigor, / the vaiśyas also carried out agricultural work, eager for food.

5.27.s:
uptakṣetraṃ sakṛccāpi saptavāraṃ lunaṃti te ..
yathartu phalino vṛkṣā yathartu kusumānvitāḥ .. 39 ..
5.27.d:
उप्तक्षेत्रं सकृच्चापि सप्तवारं लुनंति ते ..
यथर्तु फलिनो वृक्षा यथर्तु कुसुमान्विताः .. 39 ..
5.27.m: From a field sown but once, they harvest seven times; / the trees bear fruit according to the season, adorned with seasonal flowers,

agniṣṭomādikā yajñāḥ pravartaṃte sahasraśaḥ .. 6.27.40 ..

यथर्तु पत्रसंयुक्तास्तत्र स्युः सुमनोहराः ..
अग्निष्टोमादिका यज्ञाः प्रवर्तंते सहस्रशः .. 6.27.40 ..
5.27.m: And in that age they are endowed with seasonal foliage, supremely delightful. / Sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma take place by the thousands,

5.27.s:
itaretarasaṃspardhaiḥ kriyamāṇā nṛpottamaiḥ ..
brāhmaṇaiśca suraśreṣṭha svargalokamabhīpsubhiḥ .. 41 ..
5.27.d:
इतरेतरसंस्पर्धैः क्रियमाणा नृपोत्तमैः ..
ब्राह्मणैश्च सुरश्रेष्ठ स्वर्गलोकमभीप्सुभिः .. 41 ..
5.27.m: Performed by excellent kings in mutual rivalry, / and by brahmins desirous of heaven, O best of gods.

5.27.s:
tīrthayātrāṃ vrataṃ dānaṃ niyamaṃ saṃyamaṃ tathā ..
paralokamabhīpsaṃtastatra kurvaṃti mānavāḥ .. 42 ..
5.27.d:
तीर्थयात्रां व्रतं दानं नियमं संयमं तथा ..
परलोकमभीप्संतस्तत्र कुर्वंति मानवाः .. 42 ..
5.27.m: Pilgrimage to sacred fords, vows, gifts, religious observances, and self-restraint— / these the people perform there, desiring the world beyond.

5.27.s:
sahasreṇa tu varṣāṇāṃ tatra syādyauvanaṃ nṛṇām ..
sahasrapañcakaṃ yāvadūrdhvaṃ vārddhaka mucyate .. 43 ..
5.27.d:
सहस्रेण तु वर्षाणां तत्र स्याद्यौवनं नृणाम् ..
सहस्रपञ्चकं यावदूर्ध्वं वार्द्धक मुच्यते .. 43 ..
5.27.m: Youth comes to men there at a thousand years; / old age is said to begin after five thousand.

5.27.s:

कैवर्त्तमेदभिल्लाश्च चंडालाः शूद्रमानवाः .. 44 ..
5.27.m: The washerman, the leatherworker, the dancer, the reed-worker, / the fisherman, the Meda, the Bhillas, the Caṇḍālas, and the Śūdra men—

saṃbhavaṃti yuge tasminyo nisaṃsargato vibho ..

.. indra uvāca .. ..
utpattiḥ kathameteṣāmaṃtyajānāṃ dvijo ttama ..
yathāvadvada kārtsnyena atra kautūhalaṃ mahat .. 46 ..
.. bṛhaspatiruvāca .. ..

brāhmaṇyāṃ kṣatriyājjātaḥ sūta ityabhidhīyate ..

5.27.d:

तथान्ये संख्यया हीना एतेभ्यो निंदिता नराः .. 458 ..
.. इन्द्र उवाच .. ..

यथावद्वद कार्त्स्न्येन अत्र कौतूहलं महत् .. 46 ..
.. बृहस्पतिरुवाच .. ..
एतेषामष्टधा सृष्टिर्जायतेंऽत्यजसंभवा ..
योनि दोषात्सुरश्रेष्ठ जातेर्वक्ष्याम्यहं स्फुटम् .. 47 ..

सूतेन रजकश्चैव रजकेन च चर्मकृत् .. .. 48 ..
