क्षेत्रे मागधवीर्येण बुरुडो मरुदुत्तम .. 6.27.50 ..
5.27.m:
These arise in that yuga through union of wombs, O powerful one, / as well as other degraded men, despised by these.
Indra said: / How did the birth of these outcasts come about, O best of the twice-born? / Tell me truly and in full; here my curiosity is great.
Bṛhaspati said: / An eightfold creation arises from them, originating as outcasts, / due to corruption of the womb, O best of gods; I shall explain their caste clearly.
One born of a kṣatriya father in a brahmin woman is called a sūta; / by a sūta is born a washerman, and by a washerman a leatherworker.
By a leatherworker was born a dancer, designated as an outcast. / These four arose in the field, in the field of the twice-born.
Likewise, a māgadha was born by a vaiśya in a field of twice-born origin; / by the seed of a māgadha, a reed-worker was born, O best of the Maruts.

5.27.s:
buruḍena ca kaivartaḥ kaivartena ca medakaḥ ..
catvāro vaiśyasaṃbhūtā ete kṣetre dvijanmanām ..
prajāyante suraśreṣṭha savakarmasu garhitāḥ .. 51 ..
tathā śūdreṇa saṃjajñe brāhmaṇyāṃ surasattama ..
bhillākhyaścāpi bhillena caṃḍālaśca prajāyate .. 52 ..
etau dvāvapi śūdreṇa bhavato dvijasaṃbhave ..
kṣetre sarvasurādhīśa satyametanmayoditam .. 53 ..
etattretāyuge proktaṃ mayā te surasattama ..
ākarṇaya prayatnena dvāparasyādhunā sthitim .. 54 ..
lakṣāṣṭakapramāṇena tadyugaṃ parikīrtitam ..
catuḥṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ parisaṃ khyayā ..
kapiśo jāyate tatra bhagavāngaruḍadhvajaḥ .. 55 ..
dvau pādau caiva dharmasya dvau pāpasya vyavasthitau ..
tatra syādyauvanaṃ nṛṇāṃ gate varṣaśate' khile .. 56 ..
5.27.d:
बुरुडेन च कैवर्तः कैवर्तेन च मेदकः ..
चत्वारो वैश्यसंभूता एते क्षेत्रे द्विजन्मनाम् ..
प्रजायन्ते सुरश्रेष्ठ सवकर्मसु गर्हिताः .. 51 ..
तथा शूद्रेण संजज्ञे ब्राह्मण्यां सुरसत्तम ..
भिल्लाख्यश्चापि भिल्लेन चंडालश्च प्रजायते .. 52 ..
एतौ द्वावपि शूद्रेण भवतो द्विजसंभवे ..
क्षेत्रे सर्वसुराधीश सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् .. 53 ..
एतत्त्रेतायुगे प्रोक्तं मया ते सुरसत्तम ..
आकर्णय प्रयत्नेन द्वापरस्याधुना स्थितिम् .. 54 ..
लक्षाष्टकप्रमाणेन तद्युगं परिकीर्तितम् ..
चतुःषष्टिसहस्राणि वर्षाणां परिसं ख्यया ..
कपिशो जायते तत्र भगवान्गरुडध्वजः .. 55 ..
द्वौ पादौ चैव धर्मस्य द्वौ पापस्य व्यवस्थितौ ..
तत्र स्याद्यौवनं नृणां गते वर्षशते' खिले .. 56 ..
5.27.m:
By a reed-worker a fisherman was born, and by a fisherman a Meda. / These four originated from a vaiśya in the field of the twice-born; / they are born, O best of gods, despised in all acts.
Likewise, by a śūdra in a brahmin woman, O best of the gods, / was born the one called a Bhilla, and from a Bhilla is born a Caṇḍāla.
These two also arise through a śūdra in the field of twice-born origin, / O ruler of all gods; this has been spoken truly by me.
This has been declared by me concerning the Tretāyuga, O best of gods; / listen attentively now to the state of the Dvāpara.
That yuga is proclaimed to be eight hundred thousand years / and sixty-four thousand years in extent; / there the lord whose banner is Garuḍa becomes brown-hued.
Two quarters of dharma remain, and two of sin. / Youth comes to men there after a full hundred years have passed.

5.27.s:
tato'nyaiḥ samatikrāṃtairvārdhakyaṃ pañcabhiḥ śataiḥ ..
tatra satyānṛtā lokā devā bhūpāstathā pare .. 57 ..
nāryaścāpi suraśreṣṭha tatsva rūpāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..
paṃcahastapramāṇena caturhastāstathā paraṃ .. 58 ..
nātirūpeṇa saṃyuktā na ca rūpavivarjitāḥ ..
avyaktajalpakāścāpi paśavaḥ pakṣiṇo mṛgāḥ .. 59 ..
nātipuṣpaphalairyuktā vṛkṣāścāpisureśvara ..
sasyāni tāni jāyante tatra coptānikarṣukaiḥ .. 6.27.60 ..
varṣaṃti jaladāḥ kāmaṃ bhavantyoṣadhayo'khilāḥ ..
yatkiṃcidbhūtale jñānaṃ śāstraṃ vā surasattama ..
tattatra samabhāvena na satyaṃ naiva cānṛtam .. 61 ..
tīrthānāṃ ca makhānāṃ ca dvāpare surasattama ..
phalaṃ bhāvānurūpeṇa dānānāṃ ca prajāyate .. 62 ..
etattava samākhyātaṃ yugaṃ dvāparasaṃjñakam ..
mayā sarvaṃ surādhīśa yathādṛṣṭaṃ yathā śrutam .. 63 ..
5.27.d:
ततोऽन्यैः समतिक्रांतैर्वार्धक्यं पञ्चभिः शतैः ..
तत्र सत्यानृता लोका देवा भूपास्तथा परे .. 57 ..
नार्यश्चापि सुरश्रेष्ठ तत्स्व रूपाः प्रकीर्तिताः ..
पंचहस्तप्रमाणेन चतुर्हस्तास्तथा परं .. 58 ..
नातिरूपेण संयुक्ता न च रूपविवर्जिताः ..
अव्यक्तजल्पकाश्चापि पशवः पक्षिणो मृगाः .. 59 ..
नातिपुष्पफलैर्युक्ता वृक्षाश्चापिसुरेश्वर ..
सस्यानि तानि जायन्ते तत्र चोप्तानिकर्षुकैः .. 6.27.60 ..
वर्षंति जलदाः कामं भवन्त्योषधयोऽखिलाः ..
यत्किंचिद्भूतले ज्ञानं शास्त्रं वा सुरसत्तम ..
तत्तत्र समभावेन न सत्यं नैव चानृतम् .. 61 ..
तीर्थानां च मखानां च द्वापरे सुरसत्तम ..
फलं भावानुरूपेण दानानां च प्रजायते .. 62 ..
एतत्तव समाख्यातं युगं द्वापरसंज्ञकम् ..
मया सर्वं सुराधीश यथादृष्टं यथा श्रुतम् .. 63 ..
5.27.m:
Then, when five other centuries have elapsed, old age arrives. / There, people, gods, kings, and others are a mixture of truth and falsehood.
Women too, O best of gods, are described as having that nature; / their height is five cubits, and further, four cubits.
They are neither exceedingly beautiful nor devoid of beauty; / the beasts, birds, and game animals have inarticulate calls.
The trees are not overly endowed with flowers and fruits, O lord of gods; / the crops grown there are those sown by the farmers.
The clouds rain at will, and all medicinal herbs grow. / Whatever knowledge or sacred scripture exists on the face of the earth, O best of gods, / exists there in equal measure, neither entirely true nor false.
In the Dvāpara, O best of gods, the fruit of sacred fords, sacrifices, / and gifts arises in accordance with one's disposition.
This yuga named Dvāpara has been declared to you / in its entirety by me, O ruler of the gods, just as it was seen and heard.

5.27.s:
śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā vadato mama sāṃpratam ..
raudraṃ kaliyugaṃnāma yatra kṛṣṇo janārdanaḥ .. 64 ..
dvātriṃśacca sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ kathitaṃ vibho ..
tathā lakṣacatuṣkeṇa sādhulokavivarjitam ..65..
tatraikapādayuktaśca dharmaḥ pāpaṃ tribhiḥ smṛtam ..
pūrvārdhebhyaḥ paraṃ sarvaṃ saṃbhaviṣyati pāta kam .. 66 ..
na śṛṇvaṃti pituḥ putrā na snuṣā bhrātaro na ca ..
na bhṛtyā na kalatrāṇi yatra dveṣaḥ parasparam .. 67 ..
yatra ṣoḍaśame varṣe narāḥ palita yauvanāḥ ..
tatra dvādaśame varṣe garbhaṃ dhāsyati cāṃganā .. 68 ..
āyuḥ paraṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ śatasaṃkhyaṃ sureśvara ..
nāgānāṃ ca tarūṇāṃ ca varṣāṇāṃ yatra nādhikam .. 69 ..
dvātriṃśaddhayamukhyānāṃ caturviṃśatiḥ kharoṣṭrayoḥ ..
ajānāṃ ṣoḍaśa proktaṃ śunāṃ dvādaśasaṃkhyayā .. 6.27.70 ..
5.27.d:
शृणुष्वावहितो भूत्वा वदतो मम सांप्रतम् ..
रौद्रं कलियुगंनाम यत्र कृष्णो जनार्दनः .. 64 ..
द्वात्रिंशच्च सहस्राणि वर्षाणां कथितं विभो ..
तथा लक्षचतुष्केण साधुलोकविवर्जितम् ..65..
तत्रैकपादयुक्तश्च धर्मः पापं त्रिभिः स्मृतम् ..
पूर्वार्धेभ्यः परं सर्वं संभविष्यति पात कम् .. 66 ..
न शृण्वंति पितुः पुत्रा न स्नुषा भ्रातरो न च ..
न भृत्या न कलत्राणि यत्र द्वेषः परस्परम् .. 67 ..
यत्र षोडशमे वर्षे नराः पलित यौवनाः ..
तत्र द्वादशमे वर्षे गर्भं धास्यति चांगना .. 68 ..
आयुः परं मनुष्याणां शतसंख्यं सुरेश्वर ..
नागानां च तरूणां च वर्षाणां यत्र नाधिकम् .. 69 ..
द्वात्रिंशद्धयमुख्यानां चतुर्विंशतिः खरोष्ट्रयोः ..
अजानां षोडश प्रोक्तं शुनां द्वादशसंख्यया .. 6.27.70 ..
5.27.m:
Becoming attentive, listen as I speak now / of the terrible Kaliyuga, where Janārdana is black.
It is stated to last four hundred thousand / and thirty-two thousand years, O powerful one, devoid of virtuous people.
There dharma has only one quarter, while sin is remembered as having three; / after the first half, everything will become sinful.
Sons do not obey their father, nor daughters-in-law, nor brothers, / nor servants, nor wives, where there is mutual enmity.
Where men's youth turns gray in the sixteenth year, / and a woman will conceive a child in her twelfth year.
The lifespan of humans is a maximum of a hundred years, O lord of gods; / for elephants and trees, it does not exceed that number of years.
Thirty-two is stated for the best horses, twenty-four for donkeys and camels, / sixteen is declared for goats, and twelve for dogs.

5.27.s:
catuṣpadānāmanyeṣāṃ viṃśatiḥ paṃcabhiryutā ..
yatra kākāśca gṛdhrāśca kauśikāścirajīvinaḥ .. 71 ..
tathā pāpaparā lokā duḥsthitāśca viśeṣataḥ ..
tathā kaṇṭakino vṛkṣā rūkṣāḥ puṣpaphalacyutāḥ ..
sevitāste'pi gṛdhrādyairyatra cchāyāvivarjitāḥ .. 72 ..
yatra dharmo hyadharmeṇa pīḍyate surasattama ..
asatyena tathā satyaṃ bhūpāścauraiḥ sadaiva tu .. 73 ..
guravaśca tathā śiṣyaiḥ strībhiśca puruṣādhamāḥ ..
svāmino bhṛtyavargaiśca mūrkhaiścāpi bahuśrutāḥ .. 74 ..
yatra sīdaṃti dharmiṣṭhā narāḥ satyaparāyaṇāḥ ..
dāntā vivekinaḥ śāntāstathā parahite ratāḥ .. 75 ..
ādhayo vyādhayaścaiva tathā pīḍā mahādbhutā ..
sadaiva saṃsthitā yatra sādhupīḍanavāṃchayā .. 76 ..
alpāyuṣastathā martyā jāyaṃte varṇasaṃkarāt ..
ye kecana prajīvaṃti duḥkhena te samanvitāḥ ..77..
5.27.d:
चतुष्पदानामन्येषां विंशतिः पंचभिर्युता ..
यत्र काकाश्च गृध्राश्च कौशिकाश्चिरजीविनः .. 71 ..
तथा पापपरा लोका दुःस्थिताश्च विशेषतः ..
तथा कण्टकिनो वृक्षा रूक्षाः पुष्पफलच्युताः ..
सेवितास्तेऽपि गृध्राद्यैर्यत्र च्छायाविवर्जिताः .. 72 ..
यत्र धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण पीड्यते सुरसत्तम ..
असत्येन तथा सत्यं भूपाश्चौरैः सदैव तु .. 73 ..
गुरवश्च तथा शिष्यैः स्त्रीभिश्च पुरुषाधमाः ..
स्वामिनो भृत्यवर्गैश्च मूर्खैश्चापि बहुश्रुताः .. 74 ..
यत्र सीदंति धर्मिष्ठा नराः सत्यपरायणाः ..
दान्ता विवेकिनः शान्तास्तथा परहिते रताः .. 75 ..
आधयो व्याधयश्चैव तथा पीडा महाद्भुता ..
सदैव संस्थिता यत्र साधुपीडनवांछया .. 76 ..
अल्पायुषस्तथा मर्त्या जायंते वर्णसंकरात् ..
ये केचन प्रजीवंति दुःखेन ते समन्विताः ..77..
5.27.m:
For other quadrupeds it is twenty-five, / while crows, vultures, and owls live long.
People are devoted to sin and especially distressed; / the trees are thorny, rough, devoid of flowers and fruits, / and frequented by vultures and the like, where they cast no shade.
Where dharma is oppressed by adharma, O best of gods, / truth is similarly oppressed by untruth, and kings are constantly harassed by thieves;
Gurus by their disciples, base men by women, / masters by groups of servants, and scholars by fools.
Where most righteous men, devoted to truth, / self-controlled, discerning, peaceful, and intent on the welfare of others, suffer distress; 75
where mental agonies, physical diseases, and most extraordinary afflictions / are ever present out of a desire to torment the virtuous; 76
and where mortals are born short-lived as a result of the mixture of classes; / whatever individuals survive are attended by misery; 77

5.27.s:

they are heretics, engaged in forbidden deeds, and live off others' wives; / where affection arises only by taking refuge in selfish cause and effect; 86
not from natural disposition, O thousand-eyed one, among embodied beings in any way; / all classes and the twice-born will fall into the condition of mlecchas; 87

then they will suffer diminution as the Kali age advances; / and then in the end, men will become dwellers in holes; 89

all rules, self-restraints, and incantations likewise; / sacred fords will become defiled by contact with mlecchas, O Śatakratu; 91

there those will come into being, along with vile humans; / abandoning even a well-born bridegroom endowed with beauty and youth, 93
men will give their daughter to a vile man out of greed for wealth; / maidens will give birth, and maidens will be eager for sexual intercourse; 94
maidens will have union with men; / even noble-born women will deceive their husbands; 95
ill-behaved in all actions, even if guarded with great care; / and pitiless kings will oppress the cultivators; 96
they will oppress the innocent out of greed for wealth, without doubt; / and having caught a thief who deserves death, out of greed for wealth, 97
they will release him in that yuga, even though he engages in injuring living beings; / abandoning the duty of the warrior class, they will engage in battle; 98
Bṛhaspati said: / All this has been declared by me to you—the characteristic of the yugas / and their duration, O best of the gods, of all four without doubt. 99

5.28.d:
हाटकेश्वरमाहात्म्यादस्पृष्टं कलिना हि तत् ..
पंचक्रोशप्रमाणेन अचलेश्वरजेन च .. 14 ..
5.28.m: Indeed, by the greatness of Hāṭakeśvara, and of Acaleśvara, / it remains untouched by Kali over a span of five krośas. 14

5.28.s:
tasmāsvāṃśena gacchaṃtu tatra tīrthānyaśeṣataḥ ..
teṣāṃ kalibhayaṃ śakra naiva tatrāstyasaṃśayam .. 15 ..
5.28.d:
तस्मास्वांशेन गच्छंतु तत्र तीर्थान्यशेषतः ..
तेषां कलिभयं शक्र नैव तत्रास्त्यसंशयम् .. 15 ..
5.28.m: Therefore, let all the sacred fords go there with their portions; / there is certainly no fear of Kali for them there, O Śakra, without doubt." 15

5.28.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya sarvatīrthāni tatkṣaṇāt ..
hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñaṃ tatkṣetraṃ jagmurdvijottamāḥ .. 16 ..
5.28.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य सर्वतीर्थानि तत्क्षणात् ..
हाटकेश्वरसंज्ञं तत्क्षेत्रं जग्मुर्द्विजोत्तमाः .. 16 ..
5.28.m: Hearing his word, O best of brahmins, all the sacred fords immediately went to that sacred field named Hāṭakeśvara.

5.28.s:
yajñopavītamātrāṇi kṛtvā sthānāni cātmanaḥ ..
kṣetramāsādayāmāsustatsarvahi dvijottamāḥ .. 17 ..
5.28.d:
यज्ञोपवीतमात्राणि कृत्वा स्थानानि चात्मनः ..
क्षेत्रमासादयामासुस्तत्सर्वहि द्विजोत्तमाः .. 17 ..
5.28.m: Having made their places the size of a sacred thread, O best of brahmins, they all occupied that sacred field.

5.28.s:
etasmātkāraṇājāta kṣetraṃ puṇyatamaṃ hi tat ..
hāṭakeśvaradevasya mahāpātakanāśanam .. 18 ..
5.28.d:
एतस्मात्कारणाजात क्षेत्रं पुण्यतमं हि तत् ..
हाटकेश्वरदेवस्य महापातकनाशनम् .. 18 ..
5.28.m: For this reason, that sacred field of Lord Hāṭakeśvara became most holy, destroying great sins.

5.28.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
atyāścaryamidaṃ sūta yattvayaitadudāhṛtam ..
saṃgamaṃ sarvatīrthānāṃ kṣetre tatra prakīrtitam .. 19 ..
5.28.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
अत्याश्चर्यमिदं सूत यत्त्वयैतदुदाहृतम् ..
संगमं सर्वतीर्थानां क्षेत्रे तत्र प्रकीर्तितम् .. 19 ..
5.28.m: The seers said: / This is most wondrous, O Sūta, which has been spoken by you: / the gathering of all sacred fords is proclaimed in that sacred field.

5.28.s:
tāvanmātraprabhāvāṇi tatsthāni prabhavaṃti kim ..
tāni tīrthāni no brūhi vistareṇa mahāmate .. 6.28.20 ..
5.28.d:
तावन्मात्रप्रभावाणि तत्स्थानि प्रभवंति किम् ..
तानि तीर्थानि नो ब्रूहि विस्तरेण महामते .. 6.28.20 ..
5.28.m: Do those situated there possess power equal to them? / Tell us in detail about those sacred fords, O highly intelligent one,

5.28.s:
nāmataḥ sthānataścaiva tathā caiva prabhāvataḥ ..
sarvāṇyapimahābhāga paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ .. .. 21 ..
5.28.d:
नामतः स्थानतश्चैव तथा चैव प्रभावतः ..
सर्वाण्यपिमहाभाग परं कौतूहलं हि नः .. .. 21 ..
5.28.m: by name, by location, and likewise by efficacy, / all of them, O fortunate one, for our curiosity is indeed great.

5.28.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tisraḥ koṭyo'rdhakoṭiśca tīrthānāṃ dvijasattamāḥ ..
hāṭakeśvarajaṃ kṣetraṃ vyāpya sarvaṃ vyavasthitāḥ .. .. 22 ..
5.28.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तिस्रः कोट्योऽर्धकोटिश्च तीर्थानां द्विजसत्तमाः ..
हाटकेश्वरजं क्षेत्रं व्याप्य सर्वं व्यवस्थिताः .. .. 22 ..
5.28.m: Sūta said: / Three and a half crores of sacred fords, O best of brahmins, / having pervaded the entire sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara, are situated there.

5.28.s:
na teṣāṃ kīrtanaṃ śakyaṃ kartuṃ varṣaśatairapi ..
tathā svāyaṃbhuvasyādau kalpasya prathamasya ca .. 23 ..
5.28.d:
न तेषां कीर्तनं शक्यं कर्तुं वर्षशतैरपि ..
तथा स्वायंभुवस्यादौ कल्पस्य प्रथमस्य च .. 23 ..
5.28.m: It is not possible to recount them even in hundreds of years. / Likewise, in the beginning of the Svāyambhuva, the first kalpa,

5.28.s:
kṛtaḥ samāśrayastatra kṣetre tīrthaiḥ śubhāvahe ..
bahutvādatha kālasya bahūni dvijasattamāḥ .. 24 ..
5.28.d:
कृतः समाश्रयस्तत्र क्षेत्रे तीर्थैः शुभावहे ..
बहुत्वादथ कालस्य बहूनि द्विजसत्तमाः .. 24 ..
5.28.m: refuge was taken there in that auspicious sacred field by the sacred fords. / Then, through the lapse of much time, O best of brahmins,

5.28.s:
ucchedaṃ saṃprayātāni tīrthānyāyatanāni ca ..
yānyahaṃ veda kārtsnyena prabhāvasahitāni ca ..
tāni vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi śṛṇudhvaṃ susamāhitāḥ .. 25 ..
5.28.d:
उच्छेदं संप्रयातानि तीर्थान्यायतनानि च ..
यान्यहं वेद कार्त्स्न्येन प्रभावसहितानि च ..
तानि वः कीर्तयिष्यामि शृणुध्वं सुसमाहिताः .. 25 ..
5.28.m: many sacred fords and shrines have gone to destruction. / Those which I know completely, along with their powers, / I shall proclaim to you; listen attentively.

5.28.s:
yeṣāṃ saṃśravaṇādeva naraḥ pāpātpramucyate
dhyānātsnānāttathā dānātsparśanādvijasattamāḥ .. 26 ..
5.28.d:
येषां संश्रवणादेव नरः पापात्प्रमुच्यते
ध्यानात्स्नानात्तथा दानात्स्पर्शनाद्विजसत्तमाः .. 26 ..
5.28.m: Merely by hearing about them a mortal is freed from sin, / as also through meditation, ritual ablution, gifting, and touching, O best of brahmins.

5.28.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye hāṭakeśvarakṣetre sarvatīrthasamāśrayavarṇanaṃnāmāṣṭāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 28 .. .. cha ..
5.28.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रे सर्वतीर्थसमाश्रयवर्णनंनामाष्टाविंशोऽध्यायः .. 28 .. .. छ ..
5.28.m: Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter, named 'The Description of the Gathering of All Sacred Fords in Hāṭakeśvara-kṣetra,' in the Hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmya in the sixth section, the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.29.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ sarveṣu tīrtheṣu saṃsthiteṣu dvijottamāḥ ..
tatkṣetraṃ khyātimāpannaṃ samaste dharaṇītale .. 1 ..
5.29.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं सर्वेषु तीर्थेषु संस्थितेषु द्विजोत्तमाः ..
तत्क्षेत्रं ख्यातिमापन्नं समस्ते धरणीतले .. 1 ..
5.29.m: Sūta said: / When all the sacred fords were thus situated, O best of brahmins, / that sacred field attained renown over the whole surface of the earth.

5.29.s:
samastebhyastato'dūrānmunayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ ..
saṃśrayaṃti tato bhūpāstapo'rthaṃ jarayā'nvitāḥ .. 2 ..
5.29.d:
समस्तेभ्यस्ततोऽदूरान्मुनयः शंसितव्रताः ..
संश्रयंति ततो भूपास्तपोऽर्थं जरयाऽन्विताः .. 2 ..
5.29.m: From everywhere, not far away, sages of celebrated vows resort to it; / then kings accompanied by old age [resort to it] for the sake of austerity.

5.29.s:
tathā te liṃgino dāntāḥ siddhikāmāḥ samaṃtataḥ ..
samāśrayaṃti tatkṣetraṃ savartīrthasamā śrayam .. 3 ..
5.29.d:
तथा ते लिंगिनो दान्ताः सिद्धिकामाः समंततः ..
समाश्रयंति तत्क्षेत्रं सवर्तीर्थसमा श्रयम् .. 3 ..
5.29.m: Likewise, self-controlled ascetics desiring perfection from all around / resort to that sacred field, the refuge of all sacred fords.

5.29.s:
tatra siddheśvaraṃnāma liṃgamasti dvijottamāḥ ..
sarvasiddhipradaṃ nṛṇāṃ svayaṃ siddhipradāyakam.. 4 ..
5.29.d:
तत्र सिद्धेश्वरंनाम लिंगमस्ति द्विजोत्तमाः ..
सर्वसिद्धिप्रदं नृणां स्वयं सिद्धिप्रदायकम्.. 4 ..
5.29.m: There is a liṅga there named Siddheśvara, O best of brahmins, / which grants all perfections to mortals, itself bestowing perfections.

5.29.s:
nirvidya bhūtale śarvaḥ sarvavyāpī sadā śivaḥ ..
hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñe'sminkṣetre devaḥ svayaṃ sthitaḥ .. 5 ..
5.29.d:
निर्विद्य भूतले शर्वः सर्वव्यापी सदा शिवः ..
हाटकेश्वरसंज्ञेऽस्मिन्क्षेत्रे देवः स्वयं स्थितः .. 5 ..
5.29.m: Becoming indifferent to the earthly realm, Śarva, the all-pervading Sadāśiva, / the god himself, remained in this sacred field named Hāṭakeśvara.

5.29.s:
liṃgarūpeṇa bhagavānprādurbhūtaḥ svayaṃ haraḥ..
smaraṇāddarśanāccaiva sarvasiddhipradaḥ sadā ..6..
5.29.d:
लिंगरूपेण भगवान्प्रादुर्भूतः स्वयं हरः..
स्मरणाद्दर्शनाच्चैव सर्वसिद्धिप्रदः सदा ..6..
5.29.m: The Lord Hara himself became manifest in the form of a liṅga, / granting all perfections always through remembrance and darśana.

5.29.s:
siddhenārādhito yasmāttasmātsiddheśvaraḥ smṛtaḥ ..
tasyaiva varadānāddhi atraivāvasthito haraḥ .. 7 ..
5.29.d:
सिद्धेनाराधितो यस्मात्तस्मात्सिद्धेश्वरः स्मृतः ..
तस्यैव वरदानाद्धि अत्रैवावस्थितो हरः .. 7 ..
5.29.m: Because he was worshipped by a siddha, he is therefore known as Siddheśvara. / Indeed, through granting him a boon, Hara has stayed right here.

5.29.s:
yastaṃ paśyati sadbhaktyā śuciḥ spṛśati vā naraḥ ..
vāṃchitaṃ labhate sadyo yadyapi syātsudurlabham .. 8 ..
5.29.d:
यस्तं पश्यति सद्भक्त्या शुचिः स्पृशति वा नरः ..
वांछितं लभते सद्यो यद्यपि स्यात्सुदुर्लभम् .. 8 ..
5.29.m: Whatever person sees him with true devotion or, being pure, touches him, / immediately obtains what is desired, even if it be very difficult to attain.

5.29.s:
tatra siddhiṃ gatāḥ pūrvaṃ śataśaḥ puruṣā bhuvi ..
darśanātsparśanāccānye praṇāmādapare narāḥ .. 9 ..
5.29.d:
तत्र सिद्धिं गताः पूर्वं शतशः पुरुषा भुवि ..
दर्शनात्स्पर्शनाच्चान्ये प्रणामादपरे नराः .. 9 ..
5.29.m: In the past, hundreds of persons on earth attained perfection there: / some men through darśana, others through touch, and others through prostration.

5.29.s:
dakṣiṇāmūrtimāsādya mantraṃ tasya ṣaḍakṣaram ..
yo japecchraddhayopetastasyāyuḥ saṃpravardhate .. 6.29.10 ..
5.29.d:
दक्षिणामूर्तिमासाद्य मन्त्रं तस्य षडक्षरम् ..
यो जपेच्छ्रद्धयोपेतस्तस्यायुः संप्रवर्धते .. 6.29.10 ..
5.29.m: Having approached Dakṣiṇāmūrti, whoever, endowed with faith, / chants his six-syllable mantra, his lifespan increases.

5.29.s:
yāvatsaṃkhyaṃ japenmatraṃ tāvatsaṃkhyānyahāni saḥ ..
āyuṣaḥ parato martyo jīvate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 11 ..
5.29.d:
यावत्संख्यं जपेन्मत्रं तावत्संख्यान्यहानि सः ..
आयुषः परतो मर्त्यो जीवते नात्र संशयः .. 11 ..
5.29.m: For as many times as he chants the mantra, so many days / a mortal lives beyond his lifespan; there is no doubt about this.

5.29.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
atyāścaryamidaṃ sūta yattvayā parikīrtitam ..
āyuṣo'pyadhikaṃ martyo jīvate yadi mānavaḥ .. 12 ..
5.29.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
अत्याश्चर्यमिदं सूत यत्त्वया परिकीर्तितम् ..
आयुषोऽप्यधिकं मर्त्यो जीवते यदि मानवः .. 12 ..
5.29.m: The seers said: / This is most wondrous, O Sūta, which has been recounted by you, / that a human being, a mortal, may live even beyond his lifespan.

5.29.s:
.. sūta uvāca . ..
atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi svayameva mayā śrutam ..
vadatastatsamuddiśya yadvatsasya mahātmanaḥ .. 13 ..
5.29.d:
.. सूत उवाच . ..
अत्र वः कीर्तयिष्यामि स्वयमेव मया श्रुतम् ..
वदतस्तत्समुद्दिश्य यद्वत्सस्य महात्मनः .. 13 ..
5.29.m: Sūta said: / Here I shall recount to you what was heard by me myself / as the great-souled Vatsa was speaking concerning that.

5.29.s:
purā me vasamānasya purato'tra piturgṛhe ..
āyātaḥ sa munistatra vatso nāma mahādyutiḥ .. 14 ..
5.29.d:
पुरा मे वसमानस्य पुरतोऽत्र पितुर्गृहे ..
आयातः स मुनिस्तत्र वत्सो नाम महाद्युतिः .. 14 ..
5.29.m: Formerly, while I was living here in front, in my father's house, / that sage of great splendour named Vatsa arrived there,

5.29.s:
vahamāno yuvāvasthāṃ dvādaśārkasamadyutiḥ ..
aṃgaiḥ sarvaistu rūpāḍhyaḥ kāmadeva ivāparaḥ .. 15 ..
5.29.d:
वहमानो युवावस्थां द्वादशार्कसमद्युतिः ..
अंगैः सर्वैस्तु रूपाढ्यः कामदेव इवापरः .. 15 ..
5.29.m: bearing the state of youth, with splendour equal to twelve suns, / richly endowed with beauty in all his limbs, like a second Kāmadeva.

5.29.s:
matpitrā sa tadā dṛṣṭastato bhaktyā'bhivāditaḥ ..
arghyaṃ dattvā tataḥ prokto viśrāṃto vinayena ca .. 16 ..
5.29.d:
मत्पित्रा स तदा दृष्टस्ततो भक्त्याऽभिवादितः ..
अर्घ्यं दत्त्वा ततः प्रोक्तो विश्रांतो विनयेन च .. 16 ..
5.29.m: He was seen then by my father and greeted with devotion; / then, having given the water offering, he was addressed with modesty when he was rested:

5.29.s:
svāgataṃ tava vipreṃdra kutastvamiha cāgataḥ ..
ādeśo dīyatāṃ mahyaṃ kiṃ karomi yathocitam .. 17 ..
5.29.d:
स्वागतं तव विप्रेंद्र कुतस्त्वमिह चागतः ..
आदेशो दीयतां मह्यं किं करोमि यथोचितम् .. 17 ..
5.29.m: 'Welcome to you, O chief of brahmins! Whence have you come here? / Let a command be given to me. What may I do as is fitting?'

5.29.s:
.. vatsa uvāca .. ..
tavāśramapade sūta cāturmāsyasamudbhavam ..
kartumicchāmyanuṣṭhānaṃ śuśrūṣāṃ cetkaroṣi me .. 18 ..
5.29.d:
.. वत्स उवाच .. ..
तवाश्रमपदे सूत चातुर्मास्यसमुद्भवम् ..
कर्तुमिच्छाम्यनुष्ठानं शुश्रूषां चेत्करोषि मे .. 18 ..
5.29.m: Vatsa said: / 'In your hermitage, O Sūta, I wish to perform the practice / pertaining to the four months of the rainy season, if you will render me service.'

5.29.s:
.. lomaharṣaṇa uvāca .. ..
evaṃ vipra kariṣyāmi tavādeśamasaṃśayam ..
dhanyo'smyanugṛhīto'smi yastvaṃ me gṛhamāgataḥ .. 19 ..
5.29.d:
.. लोमहर्षण उवाच .. ..
एवं विप्र करिष्यामि तवादेशमसंशयम् ..
धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि यस्त्वं मे गृहमागतः .. 19 ..
5.29.m: Lomaharṣaṇa said: / 'Thus I shall do your bidding without doubt, O brahmin. / I am blessed, I am favoured, that you have come to my house.'

5.29.s:
evamuktātha māmāha sa pitā dvijasattamāḥ ..
tvayā vatsasya kartavyā śuśrūṣā nityameva hi .. 6.29.20 ..
5.29.d:
एवमुक्ताथ मामाह स पिता द्विजसत्तमाः ..
त्वया वत्सस्य कर्तव्या शुश्रूषा नित्यमेव हि .. 6.29.20 ..
5.29.m: Having spoken thus, that father of mine said to me, O best of brahmins: / 'Service to Vatsa must be rendered by you continually.'

5.29.s:
tato'haṃ vinayopetastasya kṛtyāni kṛtsnaśaḥ ..
karomi sa ca me rātrau citrāḥ kīrtayate kathāḥ .. 21 ..
5.29.d:
ततोऽहं विनयोपेतस्तस्य कृत्यानि कृत्स्नशः ..
करोमि स च मे रात्रौ चित्राः कीर्तयते कथाः .. 21 ..
5.29.m: Then I, filled with modesty, performed all his tasks completely, / and at night he recounted wondrous tales to me,

5.29.s:
rājarṣīṇāṃ purāṇānāṃ devadānavarakṣasām ..
dvīpānāṃ parvatānāṃ ca svayaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasraśaḥ .. 22 ..
5.29.d:
राजर्षीणां पुराणानां देवदानवरक्षसाम् ..
द्वीपानां पर्वतानां च स्वयं दृष्ट्वा सहस्रशः .. 22 ..
5.29.m: of royal seers of old, of gods, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas, / and of continents and mountains, having seen thousands himself.

5.29.s:
ekadā tu mayā pṛṣṭaḥ kathāṃte prāpya kautukam ..
vismayāviṣṭacittena sa dvijo dvijasattamāḥ .. 23 ..
5.29.d:
एकदा तु मया पृष्टः कथांते प्राप्य कौतुकम् ..
विस्मयाविष्टचित्तेन स द्विजो द्विजसत्तमाः .. 23 ..
5.29.m: Once, however, at the end of a narrative, having become curious, / that brahmin was asked by me whose mind was overcome with astonishment, O best of brahmins:

5.29.s:
bhagavansukumāraṃ te śarīraṃ prathamaṃ vayaḥ ..
dvīpānāṃ ca karoṣi tvaṃ kathāścitrāḥ pṛthakpṛthak .. 24 ..
5.29.d:
भगवन्सुकुमारं ते शरीरं प्रथमं वयः ..
द्वीपानां च करोषि त्वं कथाश्चित्राः पृथक्पृथक् .. 24 ..
5.29.m: 'O venerable one, your body is tender, your age is in its prime, / yet you narrate wondrous stories of the continents one by one.

5.29.s:
kathaṃ sarvaṃ dharāpṛṣṭhaṃ sasamudraṃ nirīkṣitam ..
svalpena vayasā tāta ( ?) vistarato vada .. 25 ..
5.29.d:
कथं सर्वं धरापृष्ठं ससमुद्रं निरीक्षितम् ..
स्वल्पेन वयसा तात ( ?) विस्तरतो वद .. 25 ..
5.29.m: How was the entire surface of the earth, along with the oceans, seen / at such a tender age, father? Tell me in detail.

5.29.s:
tvayā ye kīrtitā dvīpāḥ samudrāḥ parvatāstathā ..
manasāpi na śakyāste gantuṃ martyaiḥ kathaṃcana .. 26 ..
5.29.d:
त्वया ये कीर्तिता द्वीपाः समुद्राः पर्वतास्तथा ..
मनसापि न शक्यास्ते गन्तुं मर्त्यैः कथंचन .. 26 ..
5.29.m: Those continents, oceans, and mountains that have been recounted by you / cannot be reached even in thought by mortals in any way.

5.29.s:
atra kautūhalaṃ jātamaśraddheyaṃ vacastathā ..
śrutvā śraddheyavākyasya tasmātsatyaṃ prakīrtaya .. 27 ..
5.29.d:
अत्र कौतूहलं जातमश्रद्धेयं वचस्तथा ..
श्रुत्वा श्रद्धेयवाक्यस्य तस्मात्सत्यं प्रकीर्तय .. 27 ..
5.29.m: Curiosity has arisen here, hearing such an unbelievable statement / from one whose words are trustworthy; therefore tell the truth.

5.29.s:
tapasaḥ kiṃ prabhāvo'yaṃ kiṃ vā maṃtraparākramaḥ ..
yena pṛthvītalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ tvayā dṛṣṭaṃ munīśvara .. 28 ..
5.29.d:
तपसः किं प्रभावोऽयं किं वा मंत्रपराक्रमः ..
येन पृथ्वीतलं कृत्स्नं त्वया दृष्टं मुनीश्वर .. 28 ..
5.29.m: Is this the power of austerity, or the might of a mantra, / by which the whole surface of the earth was seen by you, O lord of sages?

5.29.s:
kiṃ vā devaprasādastu tavauṣadhikṛto'thavā ..
tacca puṇyatamaṃ tāta tvaṃ me brūhi savistaram .. 29 ..
5.29.d:
किं वा देवप्रसादस्तु तवौषधिकृतोऽथवा ..
तच्च पुण्यतमं तात त्वं मे ब्रूहि सविस्तरम् .. 29 ..
5.29.m: Or is it the grace of a god, or effected by an herb? / Tell me that most holy thing in full detail, dear father.'

5.29.s:
atha māṃ sa muniḥ prāha vihasya munisattamāḥ ..
satyametattvayā jñātaṃ mama maṃtraparākramam .. 6.29.30 ..
5.29.d:
अथ मां स मुनिः प्राह विहस्य मुनिसत्तमाः ..
सत्यमेतत्त्वया ज्ञातं मम मंत्रपराक्रमम् .. 6.29.30 ..
5.29.m:
Then, O best among sages, that sage smiled and said to me:
“You have rightly understood this to be the power of my mantra.

5.29.s:
sadāhamaṣṭasaṃyuktaṃ sahasraṃ śivasannidhau ..
japāmi śivamaṃtrasya ṣaḍakṣaramitasya ca .. 31 ..
5.29.d:
सदाहमष्टसंयुक्तं सहस्रं शिवसन्निधौ ..
जपामि शिवमंत्रस्य षडक्षरमितस्य च .. 31 ..
5.29.m:
I always recite one thousand and eight times in the presence of Śiva
the six-syllabled mantra of Śiva.

5.29.s:
trikālaṃ tena me jātaṃ susthiraṃ yauvanaṃ mune ..
atītānāgataṃ jñānaṃ jīvitaṃ ca sukhodayam .. 32 ..
5.29.d:
त्रिकालं तेन मे जातं सुस्थिरं यौवनं मुने ..
अतीतानागतं ज्ञानं जीवितं च सुखोदयम् .. 32 ..
5.29.m:
By virtue of that, O sage, my youth has become firmly established for the three times,
as well as knowledge of the past and future, and a life bringing forth happiness.

5.29.s:
mama varṣasahasrāṇi bahūni prayutāni ca ..
saṃjātāni mahābhāga dṛśyate prathamaṃ vayaḥ .. 33 ..
5.29.d:
मम वर्षसहस्राणि बहूनि प्रयुतानि च ..
संजातानि महाभाग दृश्यते प्रथमं वयः .. 33 ..
5.29.m:
Many thousands and millions of years have passed for me,
O fortunate one, yet my age appears to be the prime of life.

5.29.s:
atra te kīrtayiṣyāmi vistareṇa mahāmate ..
yathā siddhirmayā prāptā prasādācchaṃkarasya ca .. 34 ..
5.29.d:
अत्र ते कीर्तयिष्यामि विस्तरेण महामते ..
यथा सिद्धिर्मया प्राप्ता प्रसादाच्छंकरस्य च .. 34 ..
5.29.m:
In this matter I shall recount to you in detail, O noble-minded one,
how perfection was attained by me through the grace of Śaṃkara.

5.29.s:
ahaṃ hi brāhmaṇo nāmnā vatsaḥ khyāto mahītale ..
nānāśāstrakṛtābhyāsaḥ purā''saṃ vedapāragaḥ .. 35 ..
5.29.d:
अहं हि ब्राह्मणो नाम्ना वत्सः ख्यातो महीतले ..
नानाशास्त्रकृताभ्यासः पुरा'ऽसं वेदपारगः .. 35 ..
5.29.m:
Formerly, I was a brahmin known by the name of Vatsa on the earth,
who had practiced various scriptures and mastered the Vedas.

5.29.s:
etasminneva kāle tu menakā ca varāpsarāḥ ..
vasaṃtasamaye prāptā martyaloke yadṛcchayā .. 36 ..
5.29.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु मेनका च वराप्सराः ..
वसंतसमये प्राप्ता मर्त्यलोके यदृच्छया .. 36 ..
5.29.m:
At that very time, Menakā, an excellent apsaras,
arrived by chance in the mortal world during the spring season.

5.29.s:
sā gatā bhramamāṇātha kāmyakaṃnāma tadvanam ..
mattakokilanādāḍhyaṃ manojñadrumasaṃ kulam .. 37 ..
5.29.d:
सा गता भ्रममाणाथ काम्यकंनाम तद्वनम् ..
मत्तकोकिलनादाढ्यं मनोज्ञद्रुमसं कुलम् .. 37 ..
5.29.m:
Wandering about, she then went to that forest named Kāmyaka,
which was rich with the calls of rutting cuckoos and filled with delightful trees,

5.29.s:
yatrāste muniśārdūlo devarāta iti smṛtaḥ ..
vratasvādhyāyasaṃpannastapasā dhvastakilviṣaḥ .. 38 ..
5.29.d:
यत्रास्ते मुनिशार्दूलो देवरात इति स्मृतः ..
व्रतस्वाध्यायसंपन्नस्तपसा ध्वस्तकिल्विषः .. 38 ..
5.29.m:
where dwelt a tiger among sages known as Devarāta,
endowed with vows and Vedic recitation, his sins destroyed by austerity.

5.29.s:
upaviṣṭo nadītīre devatārccāparāyaṇaḥ ..
śraddhayā parayā yukta ekākī nirjane vane .. 39 ..
5.29.d:
उपविष्टो नदीतीरे देवतार्च्चापरायणः ..
श्रद्धया परया युक्त एकाकी निर्जने वने .. 39 ..
5.29.m:
Seated on the riverbank, devoted to worshiping the deity,
endowed with supreme faith, he was alone in the desolate forest.

5.29.s:
atha sā paśyatastasya vivastrā prāviśajjalam ..
divyarūpasamopetā gharmārtā varavarṇinī .. .. 6.29.40 ..
5.29.d:
अथ सा पश्यतस्तस्य विवस्त्रा प्राविशज्जलम् ..
दिव्यरूपसमोपेता घर्मार्ता वरवर्णिनी .. .. 6.29.40 ..
5.29.m:
Then, as he looked on, she entered the water without clothes—
that fair-complexioned woman endowed with celestial beauty, afflicted by the heat.

5.29.s:
atha tasya munīṃdrasya retaścaskanda tatkṣaṇāt ..
dṛṣṭvā tāṃ cārusarvāṃgīṃ jalamadhyaṃ samāśritām .. 41 ..
5.29.d:
अथ तस्य मुनींद्रस्य रेतश्चस्कन्द तत्क्षणात् ..
दृष्ट्वा तां चारुसर्वांगीं जलमध्यं समाश्रिताम् .. 41 ..
5.29.m:
Then the semen of that lord of sages was instantly discharged
upon seeing her, lovely in every limb, having entered the middle of the water.

5.29.s:
etasminnaṃtare prāptā sāraṃgī supipāsitā ..
jalamiśraṃ tayā retaḥ pītaṃ sarvamaśeṣataḥ .. 42 ..
5.29.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे प्राप्ता सारंगी सुपिपासिता ..
जलमिश्रं तया रेतः पीतं सर्वमशेषतः .. 42 ..
5.29.m:
Meanwhile, a very thirsty doe arrived;
she drank the semen mixed with the water, completely and without remainder.

5.29.s:
atha sā'pi dadhe garbhaṃ mānuṣaṃ vai prabhāvataḥ ..
amogharetaso māse suṣuve daśame tataḥ..43..
5.29.d:
अथ साऽपि दधे गर्भं मानुषं वै प्रभावतः ..
अमोघरेतसो मासे सुषुवे दशमे ततः..43..
5.29.m:
Then, through the power of the unfailing semen, she too bore a human fetus,
and in the tenth month she gave birth.

5.29.s:
janayāmāsa dīptāṃgī kanyāṃ padmadalekṣaṇām ..
tasminneva jale puṇye devarātāśramaṃ prati .. 44 ..
5.29.d:
जनयामास दीप्तांगी कन्यां पद्मदलेक्षणाम् ..
तस्मिन्नेव जले पुण्ये देवराताश्रमं प्रति .. 44 ..
5.29.m:
The doe with radiant limbs gave birth to a maiden with eyes like lotus petals
in that very sacred water, near Devarāta’s hermitage.

5.29.s:
atha tāṃ sa munirjñātvā svajñānena svavīryajām ..
kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo jagrāha ca pupoṣa ca .. 45 ..
5.29.d:
अथ तां स मुनिर्ज्ञात्वा स्वज्ञानेन स्ववीर्यजाम् ..
कृपया परयाविष्टो जग्राह च पुपोष च .. 45 ..
5.29.m:
Then that sage, recognizing by his inner knowledge that she was born of his own semen,
was overwhelmed with supreme compassion; he took her and raised her.

5.29.s:
snehena mahatā yuktaḥ kṛtakautukamaṃgalaḥ ..
rakṣamāṇo vane caināṃ śvāpadebhyaḥ prayatnataḥ .. 46 ...
5.29.d:
स्नेहेन महता युक्तः कृतकौतुकमंगलः ..
रक्षमाणो वने चैनां श्वापदेभ्यः प्रयत्नतः .. 46 ...
5.29.m:
Filled with great affection, having performed the auspicious rites of childhood,
he protected her with effort from beasts of prey in the forest.

5.29.s:
ājahāra sumṛṣṭāni tatkṛte suphalāni saḥ ..
svayaṃ gatvā sudūraṃ ca kānane śvāpadākule .. 47 ..
5.29.d:
आजहार सुमृष्टानि तत्कृते सुफलानि सः ..
स्वयं गत्वा सुदूरं च कानने श्वापदाकुले .. 47 ..
5.29.m:
For her sake he brought very sweet, fine fruits,
having gone far away himself in the forest teeming with beasts of prey.

5.29.s:
tatrasthā vavṛdhe sā ca nāmnā khyātā mṛgāvatī ..
śuklapakṣe yathā vyomni kaleva śaśalakṣmaṇaḥ .. 48 ..
5.29.d:
तत्रस्था ववृधे सा च नाम्ना ख्याता मृगावती ..
शुक्लपक्षे यथा व्योम्नि कलेव शशलक्ष्मणः .. 48 ..
5.29.m:
Staying there, she grew, known by the name Mṛgāvatī,
like a digit of the moon in the sky during the bright fortnight.

5.29.s:
atha sā bhramamāṇena mayā dṛṣṭā mṛgekṣaṇā ..
tato'haṃ kāmabāṇena tatkṣaṇāttāḍito hṛdi .. .. 49 ..
5.29.d:
अथ सा भ्रममाणेन मया दृष्टा मृगेक्षणा ..
ततोऽहं कामबाणेन तत्क्षणात्ताडितो हृदि .. .. 49 ..
5.29.m:
Then, as I was wandering, she of deer-like eyes was seen by me;
thereupon, I was instantly struck in the heart by the arrow of Kāma.

5.29.s:
vijñāya ca kumārīṃ tāṃ savarṇāṃ cāruhāsinīm ..
ādareṇa gṛhaṃ gatvā sa muniryācitastataḥ .. 6.29.50 ..
5.29.d:
विज्ञाय च कुमारीं तां सवर्णां चारुहासिनीम् ..
आदरेण गृहं गत्वा स मुनिर्याचितस्ततः .. 6.29.50 ..
5.29.m:
And knowing that sweet-smiling maiden to be of the same caste,
I respectfully went to his dwelling and then asked the sage:

5.29.s:
prayacchaināṃ mama brahmanpatnyarthaṃ nija kanyakām ..
yathātmā poṣayiṣyāmi bhojanācchādanādibhiḥ .. 51 ..
5.29.d:
प्रयच्छैनां मम ब्रह्मन्पत्न्यर्थं निज कन्यकाम् ..
यथात्मा पोषयिष्यामि भोजनाच्छादनादिभिः .. 51 ..
5.29.m:
“O brahmin, give this daughter of yours to me for a wife;
I will nurture her like my own self, with food, clothing, and the like.”

5.29.s:
tatastena pradattā me tatkṣaṇādeva sundarī ..
vidhinā śāstradṛṣṭena nakṣatre bhaga daivate .. 52 ..
5.29.d:
ततस्तेन प्रदत्ता मे तत्क्षणादेव सुन्दरी ..
विधिना शास्त्रदृष्टेन नक्षत्रे भग दैवते .. 52 ..
5.29.m:
Then he gave the beautiful girl to me that very moment,
according to the rule seen in the scriptures, under the constellation presided over by Bhaga.

5.29.s:
tataḥ katipayāhasya mayoḍhā sā suvismitā ..
sakhījanasamāyuktā phalārthaṃ nirgatā vane .. 53 ..
5.29.d:
ततः कतिपयाहस्य मयोढा सा सुविस्मिता ..
सखीजनसमायुक्ता फलार्थं निर्गता वने .. 53 ..
5.29.m:
Then, after a few days, she who was married by me, full of wonder,
went out into the forest with her female companions in search of fruit.

5.29.s:
atha vīrudhasaṃchanne vane tasminsusaṃsthite ..
tayā nyastaṃ padaṃ mūrdhni tṛṇācchannasya bhoginaḥ .. 54 ..
5.29.d:
अथ वीरुधसंछन्ने वने तस्मिन्सुसंस्थिते ..
तया न्यस्तं पदं मूर्ध्नि तृणाच्छन्नस्य भोगिनः .. 54 ..
5.29.m:
Now, in that forest densely covered with creepers and well established,
her foot was placed upon the head of a serpent concealed by grass.

5.29.s:
sā daṣṭā sahasā tena patitā vasudhātale ..
viṣārditā gataprāṇā tatkṣaṇādeva bhāminī .. 55 ..
5.29.d:
सा दष्टा सहसा तेन पतिता वसुधातले ..
विषार्दिता गतप्राणा तत्क्षणादेव भामिनी .. 55 ..
5.29.m:
Suddenly bitten by it, she fell to the ground;
afflicted by poison, that lovely woman lost her life that very instant.

5.29.s:
atha sakhyaḥ samāgatya tasyā duḥkhena duḥkhitāḥ ..
śaśaṃsustā yathāvṛttaṃ rudantyo mama sūtaja .. 56 ..
5.29.d:
अथ सख्यः समागत्य तस्या दुःखेन दुःखिताः ..
शशंसुस्ता यथावृत्तं रुदन्त्यो मम सूतज .. 56 ..
5.29.m:
Then her friends, gathered together, grieving with her grief,
wept and reported what had occurred to me, O son of Sūta.

5.29.s:
tato'haṃ satvaraṃ gatvā dṛṣṭvā tāṃ patitāṃ bhuvi ..
vilāpānkṛtavāndīno ruditaṃ karuṇasvaram .. 57 ..
5.29.d:
ततोऽहं सत्वरं गत्वा दृष्ट्वा तां पतितां भुवि ..
विलापान्कृतवान्दीनो रुदितं करुणस्वरम् .. 57 ..
5.29.m:
Then I went in haste, and seeing her fallen on the ground,
I, wretched, uttered laments, weeping with a plaintive voice:

5.29.s:
iyaṃ me suviśālākṣī manaḥprāṇasamā priyā ..
mṛtā bhūmau yayā hīno nāhaṃ jīvitumutsahe .. 58 ..
5.29.d:
इयं मे सुविशालाक्षी मनःप्राणसमा प्रिया ..
मृता भूमौ यया हीनो नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे .. 58 ..
5.29.m:
“This wide-eyed woman, my beloved who was equal to my mind and life,
lies dead on the earth; deprived of her, I have no desire to live.

5.29.s:
so'hamadya gamiṣyāmi paralokaṃ sahānayā ..
priyārahitaharmyasya jīvitasya ca kiṃ phalam .. 59 ..
5.29.d:
सोऽहमद्य गमिष्यामि परलोकं सहानया ..
प्रियारहितहर्म्यस्य जीवितस्य च किं फलम् .. 59 ..
5.29.m:
Today I will go to the other world along with her;
what is the use of a life, and of a mansion, bereft of the beloved?

5.29.s:
putrapautravadhūbhiśca bhṛtyavargayutasya ca ..
patnīhīnāni no rejurgṛhāṇi gṛhamedhinām .. 6.29.60 ..
5.29.d:
पुत्रपौत्रवधूभिश्च भृत्यवर्गयुतस्य च ..
पत्नीहीनानि नो रेजुर्गृहाणि गृहमेधिनाम् .. 6.29.60 ..
5.29.m:
Even with sons, grandsons, daughters-in-law, and a host of servants,
the homes of householders do not shine when bereft of a wife.

5.29.s:
yadīyaṃ karṇanetrāṃtā tanvaṃgī madhurasvarā..
na jīvati pṛthuśroṇī mariṣye' hamasaṃśayam .. 61 ..
5.29.d:
यदीयं कर्णनेत्रांता तन्वंगी मधुरस्वरा..
न जीवति पृथुश्रोणी मरिष्ये' हमसंशयम् .. 61 ..
5.29.m:
If this slender-limbed, sweet-voiced woman with broad hips,
whose eyes reach to her ears, does not live, I shall surely die.”

5.29.s:
evaṃ vilapamānasya mama sūta kulodvaha ..
āgatāḥ suhṛdaḥ sarve ruruduste'pi duḥkhitāḥ .. 62 ..
5.29.d:
एवं विलपमानस्य मम सूत कुलोद्वह ..
आगताः सुहृदः सर्वे रुरुदुस्तेऽपि दुःखिताः .. 62 ..
5.29.m:
As I was lamenting thus, O son of Sūta, uplifter of your family,
all my friends arrived, and they too wept in sorrow.

5.29.s:
ruditvā suciraṃ tatra taiḥ samaṃ mahatīṃ citām ..
kṛtvā tāṃ saṃnidhāyātha pradatto havyavāhanaḥ .. 63 ..
5.29.d:
रुदित्वा सुचिरं तत्र तैः समं महतीं चिताम् ..
कृत्वा तां संनिधायाथ प्रदत्तो हव्यवाहनः .. 63 ..
5.29.m:
Having wept for a long time there together with them, and having prepared a great pyre,
I placed her [upon it] and then set fire to it.

5.29.s:
tata ādāya māṃ kṛcchrānninyuśca svagṛhaṃ prati ..
rudantaṃ praskhalantaṃ ca muhyamānaṃ padepade .. 64 ..
5.29.d:
तत आदाय मां कृच्छ्रान्निन्युश्च स्वगृहं प्रति ..
रुदन्तं प्रस्खलन्तं च मुह्यमानं पदेपदे .. 64 ..
5.29.m:
Then, with difficulty, taking hold of me, they led me toward my own house,
as I was weeping, stumbling, and fainting at every step.

5.29.s:
tato niśāvaśeṣe'hamutthāya tvarayā'nvitaḥ ..
kāṃtāduḥkhaparītātmā gato'raṇyaṃ tadeva hi .. 65 ..
5.29.d:
ततो निशावशेषेऽहमुत्थाय त्वरयाऽन्वितः ..
कांतादुःखपरीतात्मा गतोऽरण्यं तदेव हि .. 65 ..
5.29.m:
Then, before the night was over, I arose in haste,
my soul overwhelmed by grief for my beloved, and went back to that very forest.

5.29.s:
kāmenonmattatāṃ prāpto bhramamāṇa itastataḥ ..
vilapanneva duḥkhārto vane janavivarjite .. 66 ..
5.29.d:
कामेनोन्मत्ततां प्राप्तो भ्रममाण इतस्ततः ..
विलपन्नेव दुःखार्तो वने जनविवर्जिते .. 66 ..
5.29.m:
Driven mad by desire, wandering here and there,
continually lamenting, afflicted with grief in the forest deserted by people:

5.29.s:
kva gatāsi viśālākṣi vijane'sminvihāya mām ..
nāhaṃ gṛhaṃ gamiṣyāmi mama duḥkhāya nirdayaḥ .. 67 ..
5.29.d:
क्व गतासि विशालाक्षि विजनेऽस्मिन्विहाय माम् ..
नाहं गृहं गमिष्यामि मम दुःखाय निर्दयः .. 67 ..
5.29.m:
“Where have you gone, O wide-eyed one, leaving me in this solitude?
Cruel to my grief, I will not return home.

5.29.s:
eṣo'ruṇakarasparśātsvābhāṃ tyajati caṃdramāḥ ..
niśākṣaye nirutsāho yathāhaṃ vidhinā kṛtaḥ .. 68 ..
5.29.d:
एषोऽरुणकरस्पर्शात्स्वाभां त्यजति चंद्रमाः ..
निशाक्षये निरुत्साहो यथाहं विधिना कृतः .. 68 ..
5.29.m:
At the touch of dawn's rays, this moon relinquishes its luster
at the end of night, rendered dispirited by fate just as I am.

5.29.s:
ayaṃ tanuḥ samāyāti savitā raktamaṃḍalaḥ..
nigadiṣyati me vārtāṃ nūnaṃ kaccittvadudbhavām .. 69 ..
5.29.d:
अयं तनुः समायाति सविता रक्तमंडलः..
निगदिष्यति मे वार्तां नूनं कच्चित्त्वदुद्भवाम् .. 69 ..
5.29.m:
Here rises the sun, a slender red orb;
surely he will tell me some news concerning you.

5.29.s:
gaganaṃ vyāpayansūryaḥ saṃtāpayati māṃ bhṛśam ..
bāhye cābhyaṃtare kāmaḥ kathaṃ vakṣyāmi jīvitam .. 6.29.70 ..
5.29.d:
गगनं व्यापयन्सूर्यः संतापयति मां भृशम् ..
बाह्ये चाभ्यंतरे कामः कथं वक्ष्यामि जीवितम् .. 6.29.70 ..
5.29.m:
Pervading the sky, the sun scorches me intensely;
with passion outside and inside, how shall I endure my life?

5.29.s:
karīṃdaḥ svayamabhyeti tatkucābhau samudvahan ..
kumbhau gatvā tu pṛcchāmi yadi śaṃsati tāṃ priyām .. 71 ..
5.29.d:
करींदः स्वयमभ्येति तत्कुचाभौ समुद्वहन् ..
कुम्भौ गत्वा तु पृच्छामि यदि शंसति तां प्रियाम् .. 71 ..
5.29.m:
The lord of elephants approaches of his own accord, carrying
two frontal globes resembling her breasts; I shall go and ask him if he can tell of that beloved.”

5.29.s:
evaṃ pralapamānasya mama moho mahānabhūt ..
bhāskarāṃśuprataptasya madanākulitasya ca .. 72 ..
5.29.d:
एवं प्रलपमानस्य मम मोहो महानभूत् ..
भास्करांशुप्रतप्तस्य मदनाकुलितस्य च .. 72 ..
5.29.m:
As I was lamenting in this manner, great delusion overtook me,
scorched by the sun's rays and agitated by passion.

5.29.s:
yaṃyaṃ paśyāmi tatrāhaṃ bhramamāṇo mahāvane ..
vṛkṣaṃ vā prāṇino vāpi taṃtaṃ pṛcchāmi mohataḥ .. 73 ..
5.29.d:
यंयं पश्यामि तत्राहं भ्रममाणो महावने ..
वृक्षं वा प्राणिनो वापि तंतं पृच्छामि मोहतः .. 73 ..
5.29.m:
Whatever I saw there while wandering in the great forest—
whether a tree or a living creature—I asked it out of delusion:

5.29.s:
tvaddaṃtamusalaprakhyaṃ yasyā ūruyugaṃ gaja ..
tāṃ bālāṃ vada ceddṛṣṭā dayāṃ kṛtvā mamopari .. 74
5.29.d:
त्वद्दंतमुसलप्रख्यं यस्या ऊरुयुगं गज ..
तां बालां वद चेद्दृष्टा दयां कृत्वा ममोपरि .. 74
5.29.m:
“O elephant, if you have seen that young woman whose two thighs
resemble your tusk-pestles, speak, taking pity on me!”

5.29.s:
tvayā jaṃbūka ceddṛṣṭā biṃbāphalanibhādharā ..
dayitā mama tadbrūhi śreyaste bhavitā mahat .. 75 ..
5.29.d:
त्वया जंबूक चेद्दृष्टा बिंबाफलनिभाधरा ..
दयिता मम तद्ब्रूहि श्रेयस्ते भविता महत् .. 75 ..
5.29.m: "O rose-apple tree, if you have seen my beloved / whose lips resemble the bimba fruit, then tell me; great good will be yours. / 75

5.29.s:
athavā bilva śaṃsa tvaṃ yadi bilvopamastanī ..
bhramamāṇā vane dṛṣṭā mama prāṇasamā priyā ..76..
5.29.d:
अथवा बिल्व शंस त्वं यदि बिल्वोपमस्तनी ..
भ्रममाणा वने दृष्टा मम प्राणसमा प्रिया ..76..
5.29.m: Or else, O bilva tree, declare if you have seen wandering in the forest / my beloved, equal to my very life, whose breasts resemble bilva fruits. / 76

5.29.s:
tvatpuṣpasadṛśāṃgī sā mama bhāryā manasvinī ..
sa tvaṃ caṃpaka jānīṣe yadi tvaṃ śaṃsa me drutam ..77..
5.29.d:
त्वत्पुष्पसदृशांगी सा मम भार्या मनस्विनी ..
स त्वं चंपक जानीषे यदि त्वं शंस मे द्रुतम् ..77..
5.29.m: Her limbs are like your blossoms, that wise wife of mine; / if you know [her], O campaka, tell me quickly. / 77

5.29.s:
madhūka tava puṣpeṇa dayitāyāḥ samau śubhau ..
kapolau pāṃḍuracchāyau dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ smṛtimāgatau ..78..
5.29.d:
मधूक तव पुष्पेण दयितायाः समौ शुभौ ..
कपोलौ पांडुरच्छायौ दृष्ट्वा त्वां स्मृतिमागतौ ..78..
5.29.m: O madhūka, my beloved's lovely cheeks, pale in hue, / are like your blossom; seeing you, the memory has come to me. / 78

5.29.s:
kadalīstaṃbha suvyaktaṃ priyāyāśca sukomalau ..
ūrū tvatto'pi tanvaṃgyāḥ satyenātmānamālabhe ..79..
5.29.d:
कदलीस्तंभ सुव्यक्तं प्रियायाश्च सुकोमलौ ..
ऊरू त्वत्तोऽपि तन्वंग्याः सत्येनात्मानमालभे ..79..
5.29.m: O plantain stem, clearly the thighs of my slender-limbed beloved / are far softer even than you; by truth I swear upon myself! / 79

5.29.s:
bhobho mṛga na me bhāryā tvayā dṛṣṭā'tra kānane ..
tvatsame locane spaṣṭe kajjalena samāvṛte .. 6.29.80 ..
tṛṇādo'pi suvṛddho'pi vane vṛddho'pi yaḥ paśuḥ ..
so'pi kāṃtāparityakto na mṛgo ramate kṣaṇam..8...
5.29.d:
भोभो मृग न मे भार्या त्वया दृष्टाऽत्र कानने ..
त्वत्समे लोचने स्पष्टे कज्जलेन समावृते .. 6.29.80 ..
तृणादोऽपि सुवृद्धोऽपि वने वृद्धोऽपि यः पशुः ..
सोऽपि कांतापरित्यक्तो न मृगो रमते क्षणम्..8...
5.29.m:
O deer, have you not seen my wife here in the forest? / Her distinct eyes, adorned with collyrium, are just like yours. / 6.29.80
Even a beast, a grass-eater, though very old and grown old in the forest— / even that deer, abandoned by his mate, takes no pleasure for a moment. / 81

5.29.s:
kāṃtāyāḥ purato nityaṃ vidhatteṃ'gaṃ kalāpakṛt ..
vihaṃgayoni jāto'pi vṛddhyarthaṃ puṣpadhanvanaḥ..82..
5.29.d:
कांतायाः पुरतो नित्यं विधत्तेंऽगं कलापकृत् ..
विहंगयोनि जातोऽपि वृद्ध्यर्थं पुष्पधन्वनः..82..
5.29.m: The peacock constantly displays his plumage before his mate, / though born of the avian womb, to increase the power of the flower-bowed god. / 82

5.29.s:
yo'yaṃ saṃdṛśyate haṃso haṃsīmanusmaratyasau ..
gatistādṛṅna cāpyasya matpriyāyāśca yādṛśī ..83..
5.29.d:
योऽयं संदृश्यते हंसो हंसीमनुस्मरत्यसौ ..
गतिस्तादृङ्न चाप्यस्य मत्प्रियायाश्च यादृशी ..83..
5.29.m: This swan who is seen here longs for his mate; / but his gait is not like the gait of my beloved. / 83

5.29.s:
eka eva sudhanyo'yaṃ cakravāko vihaṃgamaḥ ..
muhūrtamapi yo'bhīṣṭāṃ na tyajeccakravākikām .. 84 ..
5.29.d:
एक एव सुधन्योऽयं चक्रवाको विहंगमः ..
मुहूर्तमपि योऽभीष्टां न त्यजेच्चक्रवाकिकाम् .. 84 ..
5.29.m: Most fortunate is this cakravāka bird alone, / who does not leave his beloved female cakravāka even for an instant. / 84

5.29.s:
ya eṣa śrūyate rāvo vibhramaṃ janayanmama ..
kiṃvā pikasamuttho 'yaṃ kiṃ vā me dayitodbhavaḥ.. 85 ..
5.29.d:
य एष श्रूयते रावो विभ्रमं जनयन्मम ..
किंवा पिकसमुत्थो ऽयं किं वा मे दयितोद्भवः.. 85 ..
5.29.m: This cry that is heard, causing me delirium— / has it arisen from a cuckoo, or has it arisen from my beloved? / 85

5.29.s:
māṃ dṛṣṭvā'yaṃ mṛgo yāti taṃ mṛgī yāti pṛṣṭhataḥ ..
dhāvamānā mamāpyevamanuyāti purā priyā ..86..
5.29.d:
मां दृष्ट्वाऽयं मृगो याति तं मृगी याति पृष्ठतः ..
धावमाना ममाप्येवमनुयाति पुरा प्रिया ..86..
5.29.m: Seeing me, this deer runs away, and the female deer follows behind him; / running thus, my beloved also used to follow me in the past. / 86

5.29.s:
vāraṇo'yaṃ priyāṃ kāṃtāmanurāgānuyāyinīm ..
sparśayatyagrahastena mama saṃsmārayanpriyāma .. 87 ..
5.29.d:
वारणोऽयं प्रियां कांतामनुरागानुयायिनीम् ..
स्पर्शयत्यग्रहस्तेन मम संस्मारयन्प्रियाम .. 87 ..
5.29.m: This elephant touches with the tip of his trunk his cherished mate / who follows him out of love, reminding me of my beloved. / 87

5.29.s:
hā priye mṛgaśāvākṣi taptakāṃcanasaṃnibhe ..
kathaṃ māṃ na vijānāsi bhramaṃtamiha kānane .. 88 ..
5.29.d:
हा प्रिये मृगशावाक्षि तप्तकांचनसंनिभे ..
कथं मां न विजानासि भ्रमंतमिह कानने .. 88 ..
5.29.m: Alas, my beloved, with eyes like a fawn's, resembling molten gold! / How do you not recognise me wandering here in the forest? / 88

5.29.s:
kva sā bhaktiḥ kva sā prītiḥ kva sā tuṣṭiḥ kva sā dayā ..
nigadantaṃ sudīnaṃ māṃ saṃbhāṣayasi no yataḥ .. 89 ..
5.29.d:
क्व सा भक्तिः क्व सा प्रीतिः क्व सा तुष्टिः क्व सा दया ..
निगदन्तं सुदीनं मां संभाषयसि नो यतः .. 89 ..
5.29.m: Where is that devotion, where is that affection, where is that satisfaction, where is that compassion? / For you do not answer me as I lament so piteously!" / 89

5.29.s:
evaṃ pralapamānasya mama prāptāḥ suhṛjjanāḥ ..
anveṣaṃtaḥ padaṃ tatra vaneṣu viṣameṣu ca .. 6.29.90 ..
5.29.d:
एवं प्रलपमानस्य मम प्राप्ताः सुहृज्जनाः ..
अन्वेषंतः पदं तत्र वनेषु विषमेषु च .. 6.29.90 ..
5.29.m: As I was lamenting thus, my kinsmen arrived, / searching for my footprints there in the rugged forests. / 6.29.90

5.29.s:
tatastaiḥ koparaktākṣaiḥ prokto'haṃ sūtanaṃdana ..
bhartsadbhiḥ paruṣairvākyairdhiktvāṃ kāmamayādhunā .. 91 ..
5.29.d:
ततस्तैः कोपरक्ताक्षैः प्रोक्तोऽहं सूतनंदन ..
भर्त्सद्भिः परुषैर्वाक्यैर्धिक्त्वां काममयाधुना .. 91 ..
5.29.m: Then, their eyes red with anger, O son of Sūta, / rebuking me with harsh words, they said: "Fie on you, now full of lust! / 91

5.29.s:
tvaṃ kiṃ śocasi mūḍhātmannaśocyaṃ jīvitaṃ nṛṇām ..
yatastvāmapi śocaṃtaṃ śocayiṣyaṃti cāpare .. 92..
5.29.d:
त्वं किं शोचसि मूढात्मन्नशोच्यं जीवितं नृणाम् ..
यतस्त्वामपि शोचंतं शोचयिष्यंति चापरे .. 92..
5.29.m: Why do you grieve, foolish-minded one, over the life of men, which is not to be grieved over? / For others will grieve for you too, who are now grieving. / 92

5.29.s:
yūyaṃ vayaṃ tathā cānye saṃjātāḥ prāṇino bhuvi ..
sarva eva mariṣyāmastatra kā paridevanā .. 93 ..
5.29.d:
यूयं वयं तथा चान्ये संजाताः प्राणिनो भुवि ..
सर्व एव मरिष्यामस्तत्र का परिदेवना .. 93 ..
5.29.m: You, we, and all other living beings born on earth— / every single one of us shall die; what lamentation can there be over that? / 93

5.29.s:
adarśanātpriyā prāptā punaścādarśanaṃ gatā ..
na sā tava na tasyāstvaṃ vṛthā kimanuśocasi .. 94 ..
5.29.d:
अदर्शनात्प्रिया प्राप्ता पुनश्चादर्शनं गता ..
न सा तव न तस्यास्त्वं वृथा किमनुशोचसि .. 94 ..
5.29.m: From invisibility your beloved came, and to invisibility she has gone again. / She is not yours, nor are you hers; why do you grieve in vain? / 94

5.29.s:
nāyamatyaṃtasaṃvāsaḥ kasyacitkenacitsaha ..
api svena śarīreṇa kimutānyairvṛthā janaiḥ .. 95 ..
5.29.d:
नायमत्यंतसंवासः कस्यचित्केनचित्सह ..
अपि स्वेन शरीरेण किमुतान्यैर्वृथा जनैः .. 95 ..
5.29.m: This dwelling together of anyone with anyone is not permanent— / even with one's own body, let alone with other people in vain! / 95

5.29.s:
mṛtaṃ vā yadi vā naṣṭaṃ yotītamanuśocati ..
sa duḥkhena labhedduḥkhaṃ dvāvanartho prapadyate .. 96 ..
5.29.d:
मृतं वा यदि वा नष्टं योतीतमनुशोचति ..
स दुःखेन लभेद्दुःखं द्वावनर्थो प्रपद्यते .. 96 ..
5.29.m: Whether dead or lost, whoever grieves for what is gone / attains sorrow upon sorrow and incurs two evils." / 96

5.29.s:
evaṃ saṃbodhayitvā māṃ gṛhītvā te muhurjanaiḥ ..
ninyu rgṛhaṃ tataḥ sarve vanāttasmātsudāruṇāt .. 97 ..
5.29.d:
एवं संबोधयित्वा मां गृहीत्वा ते मुहुर्जनैः ..
निन्यु र्गृहं ततः सर्वे वनात्तस्मात्सुदारुणात् .. 97 ..
5.29.m: Having admonished me thus and seized me repeatedly with the help of the people, / they all led me home from that dreadful forest. / 97

5.29.s:
tato mama gṛhasthasya smaramāṇasya tāṃ priyām ..
utpannaḥ sumahānkopaḥ sarpānprati mahāmate .. 98 ..
5.29.d:
ततो मम गृहस्थस्य स्मरमाणस्य तां प्रियाम् ..
उत्पन्नः सुमहान्कोपः सर्पान्प्रति महामते .. 98 ..
5.29.m: Then, as I stayed at home remembering that beloved, / a very great rage arose [in me] against serpents, O noble-minded one. / 98

5.29.s:
tataḥ kopaparītena pratijñātaṃ mayā sphuṭam ..
sarpānuddiśya yatsarvaṃ tannibodhaya dāruṇam .. 99 ..
5.29.d:
ततः कोपपरीतेन प्रतिज्ञातं मया स्फुटम् ..
सर्पानुद्दिश्य यत्सर्वं तन्निबोधय दारुणम् .. 99 ..
5.29.m: Then, overcome with anger, I clearly swore a vow / concerning all serpents; hear that dreadful [vow]: / 99

5.29.s:
adyaprabhṛti cennāhaṃ sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam ..
nihanmi daṇḍaghātena tatpāpaṃ syāddhruvaṃ mama .. 6.29.100 ..
5.29.d:
अद्यप्रभृति चेन्नाहं सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् ..
निहन्मि दण्डघातेन तत्पापं स्याद्ध्रुवं मम .. 6.29.100 ..
5.29.m: "From this day forward, if I do not strike down with a blow of a stick / any serpent that comes within range of my sight, may that sin surely be mine: / 6.29.100

5.29.s:
yacca nikṣepahartṝṇāṃ yacca viśvāsaghātinām ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 101 ..
5.29.d:
यच्च निक्षेपहर्तॄणां यच्च विश्वासघातिनाम् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 101 ..
5.29.m: Whatever [sin belongs] to thieves of deposits and whatever to betrayers of trust— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 101

5.29.s:
yatpāpaṃ sādhuniṃdāyāṃ mātāpitṛvadhe ca yat ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 102 ..
5.29.d:
यत्पापं साधुनिंदायां मातापितृवधे च यत् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 102 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin lies in reviling the virtuous, and whatever in killing mother and father— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 102

5.29.s:
paradāraratānāṃ ca yatpāpaṃ jīvaghātinām ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 103 ..
5.29.d:
परदाररतानां च यत्पापं जीवघातिनाम् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 103 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to those devoted to another's wife and to the slayers of living beings— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 103

5.29.s:
uktau cābhiratānāṃ ca yatpāpaṃ garadāyinām ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 104 ..
5.29.d:
उक्तौ चाभिरतानां च यत्पापं गरदायिनाम् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 104 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to those who delight in slander and to poisoners— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 104

5.29.s:
kṛtaghnānāṃ ca yatpāpaṃ paravittāpahāriṇām ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 105 ..
5.29.d:
कृतघ्नानां च यत्पापं परवित्तापहारिणाम् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 105 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to the ungrateful and to stealers of others' wealth— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 105

5.29.s:
yatpāpaṃ śastrakartṛṇāṃ tathā vahnipradāyinām..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 106 ..
5.29.d:
यत्पापं शस्त्रकर्तृणां तथा वह्निप्रदायिनाम्..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 106 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to wielders of weapons [against the innocent] and to incendiaries— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 106

5.29.s:
vratabhaṃgena yatpāpaṃ vratināṃ niṃdayāpi yat ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 107 ..
5.29.d:
व्रतभंगेन यत्पापं व्रतिनां निंदयापि यत् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 107 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin comes from breaking a vow and also from reviling those who observe vows— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 107

5.29.s:
yatpāpaṃ bhrūṇahatyāyāṃ mṛṣṭamāṃsāśināṃ ca yat ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 108 ..
5.29.d:
यत्पापं भ्रूणहत्यायां मृष्टमांसाशिनां च यत् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 108 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin lies in destroying an embryo, and whatever belongs to those who feast on savory meat— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 108

5.29.s:
vṛkṣaccheda prasaktānāṃ yatpāpaṃ śalyakāriṇām ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 109 ..
5.29.d:
वृक्षच्छेद प्रसक्तानां यत्पापं शल्यकारिणाम् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 109 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to those intent on felling trees and to thorn-makers— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 109

5.29.s:
pākhaṃḍināṃ ca yatpāpaṃ nāstikānāṃ ca yadbhavet ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 6.29.110 ..
5.29.d:
पाखंडिनां च यत्पापं नास्तिकानां च यद्भवेत् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 6.29.110 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to heretics and whatever belongs to atheists— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 6.29.110

5.29.s:
māṃsamadyaprasaktānāṃ yatpāpaṃ viṭabhojinām ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 111 ..
5.29.d:
मांसमद्यप्रसक्तानां यत्पापं विटभोजिनाम् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 111 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to those addicted to meat and liquor and to eaters of feces— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 111

5.29.s:
mṛṣāvādaprasaktānāṃ pararaṃdhrāvalokinām ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 112 ..
5.29.d:
मृषावादप्रसक्तानां पररंध्रावलोकिनाम् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 112 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to those addicted to lying and to seekers of others' faults— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 112

5.29.s:
yatpāpaṃ sākṣyakartṛṇāṃ dhānyasaṃgrahakāriṇām ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 113 ..
5.29.d:
यत्पापं साक्ष्यकर्तृणां धान्यसंग्रहकारिणाम् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 113 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to [false] witnesses and to hoarders of grain— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 113

5.29.s:
ākheṭakaratānāṃ ca yatpāpaṃ pāśadāyinām ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 114 ..
5.29.d:
आखेटकरतानां च यत्पापं पाशदायिनाम् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 114 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to those addicted to hunting and to set-net trappers— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 114

5.29.s:
nityaṃ preṣaṇakartṝṇāṃ yatpāpaṃ madhujīvinām ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. .. 115 ..
5.29.d:
नित्यं प्रेषणकर्तॄणां यत्पापं मधुजीविनाम् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. .. 115 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to those constantly sending others [on harsh errands] and to those who live by gathering honey— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 115

5.29.s:
adṛṣṭadevavaktrāṇāṃ yatpāpaṃ matsyajīvinām ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 116 ..
5.29.d:
अदृष्टदेववक्त्राणां यत्पापं मत्स्यजीविनाम् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 116 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to those who never look upon the face of God and to those who live by fishing— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight! / 116

5.29.s:
vivāde pṛcchamānānāṃ pakṣapātena jalpatām ..
bhayādvā yadi vā lobhāddveṣādvā kāmato'pi vā .. 117 ..
5.29.d:
विवादे पृच्छमानानां पक्षपातेन जल्पताम् ..
भयाद्वा यदि वा लोभाद्द्वेषाद्वा कामतोऽपि वा .. 117 ..
5.29.m: When questioned in a dispute, to those who speak with partiality / out of fear, or out of greed, or out of malice, or even out of lust— / 117

5.29.s:
yatpāpaṃ tu bhavetteṣāṃ nirdayānāṃ durātmanām ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 118 ..
5.29.d:
यत्पापं तु भवेत्तेषां निर्दयानां दुरात्मनाम् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 118 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to those merciless, wicked-hearted ones— / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within range of my sight!" / 118

5.29.s:
kanyāvikrayakartṛṇāṃ yatpāpaṃ pāpasaṃginām ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 119 ..
5.29.d:
कन्याविक्रयकर्तृणां यत्पापं पापसंगिनाम् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 119 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin attaches to those sinful people who sell their daughters / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within my sight.

5.29.s:
vidyāvikrayakartṝṇāṃ yatpāpaṃ samudāhṛtam ..
tanme syādyadi no hanmi sarpaṃ dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatam .. 6.29.120 ..
5.29.d:
विद्याविक्रयकर्तॄणां यत्पापं समुदाहृतम् ..
तन्मे स्याद्यदि नो हन्मि सर्पं दृष्टिवशं गतम् .. 6.29.120 ..
5.29.m: Whatever sin is proclaimed of those who sell sacred knowledge / may that be mine if I do not slay a serpent that comes within my sight.

5.29.s:
evaṃ mayā pratijñāya kopāviṣṭena sūtaja ..
gṛhīto laguḍaḥ sthūlo vadhārthaṃ pavanāśinām .. 121 ..
5.29.d:
एवं मया प्रतिज्ञाय कोपाविष्टेन सूतज ..
गृहीतो लगुडः स्थूलो वधार्थं पवनाशिनाम् .. 121 ..
5.29.m: Having thus made a vow, overcome with anger, O son of Sūta, / I took up a thick club for the sake of slaying the breath-eaters (serpents).

5.29.s:
tataḥprabhṛtyahaṃ bhūmau bhramāmi laguḍāyudhaḥ ..
brāhmīṃ vṛttiṃ parityajya mārgamāṇo bhujaṃgamān .. 122 ..
5.29.d:
ततःप्रभृत्यहं भूमौ भ्रमामि लगुडायुधः ..
ब्राह्मीं वृत्तिं परित्यज्य मार्गमाणो भुजंगमान् .. 122 ..
5.29.m: From then on I wandered the earth, armed with a club, / abandoning the brahmin's way of life and searching for serpents.

5.29.s:
mayā kopaparītena bahavaḥ pannagā hatāḥ ..
viṣolbaṇā mahākāyāstathānye madhyamādhamāḥ .. 123 ..
5.29.d:
मया कोपपरीतेन बहवः पन्नगा हताः ..
विषोल्बणा महाकायास्तथान्ये मध्यमाधमाः .. 123 ..
5.29.m: Filled with wrath, I killed many serpents, / terrible with poison, huge in body, and others middling and low.

5.29.s:
ekadāhaṃ vanaṃ prāpto gahanaṃ laguḍāyudhaḥ ..
śayānaṃ tatra cāpaśyaṃ jalasarpaṃ vayo'dhikam .. 124 ..
5.29.d:
एकदाहं वनं प्राप्तो गहनं लगुडायुधः ..
शयानं तत्र चापश्यं जलसर्पं वयोऽधिकम् .. 124 ..
5.29.m: Once, armed with my club, I reached a dense forest / and saw lying there an aged water-serpent.

5.29.s:
tato'haṃ daṃḍamudyamya kāladaṃḍopamaṃ ruṣā ..
hanmi taṃ yāvadevāhaṃ sa māṃ provāca pannagaḥ .. 125 ..
5.29.d:
ततोऽहं दंडमुद्यम्य कालदंडोपमं रुषा ..
हन्मि तं यावदेवाहं स मां प्रोवाच पन्नगः .. 125 ..
5.29.m: Then, raising my staff like the rod of Death, in rage, / as I was just about to kill him, that serpent spoke to me:

5.29.s:
nāparādhyāmi te kiṃcidahaṃ brāhmaṇasattama ..
saṃraṃbhāttatkimarthaṃ māṃ jighāṃsasi vayo'dhikam .. 126 ..
5.29.d:
नापराध्यामि ते किंचिदहं ब्राह्मणसत्तम ..
संरंभात्तत्किमर्थं मां जिघांससि वयोऽधिकम् .. 126 ..
5.29.m: "I have done you no wrong, O best of brahmins! / Why then do you, in such fury, seek to kill me who am advanced in age?"

5.29.s:
tato mayā sa saṃproktaḥ kopātsalilapannagaḥ ..
mahāmanyuparītena smṛtvā bhāryāṃ mṛgāvatīm ..
mama bhāryā priyā pūrvaṃ sarpeṇāsīdvināśitā ..127 ..
5.29.d:
ततो मया स संप्रोक्तः कोपात्सलिलपन्नगः ..
महामन्युपरीतेन स्मृत्वा भार्यां मृगावतीम् ..
मम भार्या प्रिया पूर्वं सर्पेणासीद्विनाशिता ..127 ..
5.29.m: Then I said to that water-serpent in anger, / seized by great grief upon remembering my wife Mṛgāvatī: / "Formerly my beloved wife was destroyed by a serpent.

5.29.s:
tato'haṃ tena vaireṇa sūdayāmi maho ragān ..
adya tvāmapi neṣyāmi vaivasvatagṛhaṃ prati ..
hatvā daṃḍaprahāreṇa tasmādiṣṭatamaṃ smara ..128..
5.29.d:
ततोऽहं तेन वैरेण सूदयामि महो रगान् ..
अद्य त्वामपि नेष्यामि वैवस्वतगृहं प्रति ..
हत्वा दंडप्रहारेण तस्मादिष्टतमं स्मर ..128..
5.29.m: Therefore, out of that enmity, I slaughter the great serpents. / Today I will send you too to the house of Yama, son of Vivasvat, / killing you with a blow of my staff; therefore remember your most cherished deity!"

5.29.s:
tataḥ sa māṃ punaḥ prāha bhayena mahatāvṛtaḥ..
śṛṇu tāvadvaco'smākaṃ tataḥ kuru yathocitam ..129..
5.29.d:
ततः स मां पुनः प्राह भयेन महतावृतः..
शृणु तावद्वचोऽस्माकं ततः कुरु यथोचितम् ..129..
5.29.m: Then he spoke to me again, overcome by great fear: / "First hear my words, and then do as you see fit.

5.29.s:
anye te pannagā vipra ye daśaṃtīha mānavān ..
vayaṃ salilasaṃbhūtā nirviṣāḥ sarparūpiṇaḥ .. 6.29.130 ..
5.29.d:
अन्ये ते पन्नगा विप्र ये दशंतीह मानवान् ..
वयं सलिलसंभूता निर्विषाः सर्परूपिणः .. 6.29.130 ..
5.29.m: Those are other serpents, O brahmin, that bite human beings in this world; / we are born of water, free from venom, merely serpent in form."

5.29.s:
evaṃ prajalpamāno'pi sa daṃḍena mayā hataḥ ..
sūta tatsūdanārthāya nirvikalpena cetasā .. 131 ..
5.29.d:
एवं प्रजल्पमानोऽपि स दंडेन मया हतः ..
सूत तत्सूदनार्थाय निर्विकल्पेन चेतसा .. 131 ..
5.29.m: Though he spoke thus, O Sūta, he was struck by me with my staff / with an unhesitating mind, for the purpose of slaying him.

5.29.s:
athāsau laguḍasparśāttatkṣaṇādeva pannagaḥ..
dvādaśārkapratīkāśo babhūva puruṣo mahān.. 132 ..
5.29.d:
अथासौ लगुडस्पर्शात्तत्क्षणादेव पन्नगः..
द्वादशार्कप्रतीकाशो बभूव पुरुषो महान्.. 132 ..
5.29.m: Then, from the touch of the club, instantly that serpent / became a great person resplendent like twelve suns.

5.29.s:
tadāścaryaṃ samālokya tato'haṃ vismayānvitaḥ ..
uktavāṃstaṃ praṇamyoccaiḥ kṣamyatāmiti sādaram .. 133 ..
5.29.d:
तदाश्चर्यं समालोक्य ततोऽहं विस्मयान्वितः ..
उक्तवांस्तं प्रणम्योच्चैः क्षम्यतामिति सादरम् .. 133 ..
5.29.m: Beholding that wonder, filled with astonishment, / I bowed down deeply to him and said respectfully, "Forgive me!

5.29.s:
ko bhavānkimidaṃ rūpaṃ kṛtaṃ sarpamayaṃ vibho ..
kiṃ vā te brahmaśāpo'yaṃ kiṃ vā krīḍāsadedṛśī .. 134 ..
5.29.d:
को भवान्किमिदं रूपं कृतं सर्पमयं विभो ..
किं वा ते ब्रह्मशापोऽयं किं वा क्रीडासदेदृशी .. 134 ..
5.29.m: Who are you? Why was this serpent-form assumed by you, O lord? / Or was this a curse of a brahmin, or was it some kind of sport?"

5.29.s:
tataḥ provāca māṃ hṛṣṭaḥ sa naraḥ praśrayānvitaḥ..
śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā vṛttāṃtaṃ svaṃ vadāmi te .. 135 ..
5.29.d:
ततः प्रोवाच मां हृष्टः स नरः प्रश्रयान्वितः..
शृणुष्वावहितो भूत्वा वृत्तांतं स्वं वदामि ते .. 135 ..

known as Śrīvardhana, who had exerted himself in various scriptures. / Seeing his guru coiled around on all sides by the coils of the serpent,
and realizing that I, standing not far off, was the doer of that deed, / he spoke harsh words, his eyes reddened with anger:
With both lips trembling and a voice choked with tears: / 'If I have performed good austerity through constant service to my guru,
and if Maheśvara has been meditated upon with an unwavering mind, / by that truth, may this wicked, sinful, lowest of brahmins, / by whom my guru was insulted, swiftly take on such a body!'
Then at that very instant I attained the dreadful state of a serpent, / while all the people looked on, saying, 'Well done! Well done!'
Then, having reached the end of his samādhi, the self-controlled sage / saw resting upon his own body a two-tongued creature of dreadful form.
Then [he saw] me, in the form of a serpent, filled with great sorrow, / and likewise all the people standing nearby, terrified with fear.

5.29.m:
Then, knowing all that through his eye of wisdom, / the sage, overcome with compassion, spoke angrily to his disciple Śrīvardhana:
'Disciple, you have not done what is pleasing to me by performing this deed, / cursing a wretched brahmin; this is not the duty of ascetics.
Equal in honor and dishonor, seeing a lump of earth, a stone, and gold as the same, / regarding friend and foe alike—such an ascetic attains perfection.
Therefore, my child, this brahmin was cursed by you unwittingly / out of childishness; by my command, favor should be extended to him once again.'
Then Śrīvardhana, bowing down to his guru, / overcome by indignation, stood with joined palms and said:
'Whether from ignorance or knowledge, the word that has been spoken by me / is indeed so; there is no doubt. Therefore, O guru, keep silent.
No false word has ever been uttered by me, even in jest, O guru; / how much less when it concerns your welfare! Therefore, practice silence.

5.29.m:
The sun may rise in the west, the great ocean may dry up, / and even Mount Meru may crumble, but my word shall not prove otherwise.'
To that disciple, the guru spoke again in gentle words: / 'I know that your word can never become otherwise.
A disciple, even when grown of age, must always be carefully instructed; / how much more so when you are still a boy! Therefore, I speak to you repeatedly.
No one exhausts the previously accumulated virtue of sages; / but for those deprived of austerity and virtue, no [good] destination exists.
Forbearance alone is said to grant perfection, especially to ascetics.
Therefore, placing forbearance foremost, ascetics must conduct themselves.
One should not be evil toward evil; this is the eternal wisdom. / The sinner who commits evil is destroyed by his own self.
Bereft of right knowledge, he who repays evil with evil / burns that which is already burned and strikes that which is already slain.

What virtue is there in his goodness, who is good to those who help? / He alone is praised by people who is good to those who do harm.'
Having spoken thus to that disciple, Suvrata of laudable vows, / filled with supreme compassion, then spoke this to me:
'The word of my disciple will not be otherwise, O serpent. / Therefore, remaining in the body of a serpent, wait for some time.'
The serpent said: / 'At what time, O best of sages, will my curse come to an end? / Show favor to me, wretched and ignorant of the curse.'
Suvrata said: / 'He who performs singing and other [arts] in the abode of Śiva, even for a moment— / the measure of his merit cannot be calculated, good sir.
And he who creates an obstacle in a great festival, even for a moment— / the measure of his sin indeed cannot be calculated by anyone.
Therefore you, a sinful brahmin, will not attain liberation / through mere conversation, O evil-minded one; therefore, listen to my words.

Whoever, endowed with faith, recites the six-syllabled Śaiva mantra, / even the sin born of slaying a brahmin is destroyed for him.
With ten [repetitions] a man washes away sin born of a day; with twenty, that of a year, / by the recitation of the six-syllabled [mantra].
Therefore, staying within the water, recite that mantra with reverence, / by which sin, even committed in another birth, goes to destruction.
When, while you are in the water, a twice-born named Vatsa strikes you / in anger with a stick, then you shall attain liberation.
Therefore, go quickly from this place, O serpent, to a reservoir of water.' / Having spoken what was agreeable to me, that good sage fell silent.
Then, filled with sorrow, I arrived here at this reservoir of water, / and constantly remained reciting the six-syllabled mantra.
By your favor, O best of brahmins, I am freed from the state of a serpent. / What pleasant thing may I do for you today? Therefore, speak quickly.

You are indeed he named Vatsa who was described to me / by Suvrata, without doubt. Behold, this aerial chariot approaches for me.'
Then that serpent, who had assumed a divine form, was properly addressed by me: / 'O venerable one, give me some auspicious instruction,
by which sorrow arising from the loss of dear ones does not arise, / nor poverty, nor disease, nor defeat by enemies.'
Then that excellent person, full of eagerness, spoke to me again: / 'A heavy burden of questions has been posed by you to me, O best of the twice-born.
And this cannot be spoken of at length when the aerial chariot has arrived. / Therefore, I shall tell you briefly, O twice-born.
The six-syllabled Śaiva mantra removes inauspiciousness for men. / That should be recited by you according to your capacity, O brahmin, day and night.
Then, without doubt, you will attain whatever you desire in your mind— / whether heaven or liberation—freed from all sins.

Indeed, very great sin was constantly committed by me; / yet even then, by the greatness of the mantra, worlds of great glory have been attained.
One man bestows all gifts, endowed with faith; / another recites the six-syllabled mantra: the fruit is equal for both of them.
Another man performs ritual ablutions at all sacred fords, O twice-born, / and another recites the six-syllabled mantra: the fruit is equal for both of them.'
Another performs a thousand cāndrāyaṇa penances properly; / another repeats the six-syllable mantra—their fruit is equal.
A man sleeps under the open sky in the rainy season, dwells in water during the cold season, / and practices the five fires austerity in summer for a hundred years;
another mortal, pure and filled with faith, / repeats the six-syllable mantra day and night—the fruit is considered equal for both.
One constantly performs the śrāddha rite at Gayā during the fortnight of the ancestors; / another repeats the six-syllable mantra—their fruit is equal.

5.29.m:
One gives a thousand cows at Jyeṣṭhapuṣkara on the full moon of Kārttika; / another repeats the six-syllable mantra—their fruit is equal.
One man bathes at the Saṃnihitī pool when the sun is seized by Rāhu; / but another repeats the six-syllable mantra—that is indeed equal.
Another gazes upon Somanātha on a Monday during a lunar eclipse; / another repeats the six-syllable mantra—their fruit is equal.
One man beholds Caṇḍīśvara during the northern solstice; / another repeats the six-syllable mantra—their fruit is equal.
One falls down a cliff after beholding Kedāra with devotion; / another repeats the six-syllable mantra—their fruit is equal.
Another burns dried cow dung after giving away all his possessions from the start; / another repeats the six-syllable mantra—their fruit is equal.
One attains knowledge after abandoning all attachment; / another repeats the six-syllable mantra—their fruit is equal.
